544248|2026-06.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.
544248|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR144.33 crore versus INR22.62 crore a year ago and INR83.25 crore in Q4 FY26, with GMV of about INR252 crore disclosed for the first time. EBITDA rose to INR8.92 crore and PAT to INR6.17 crore, but margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to investment in new verticals, hiring and technology. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR500-plus crore and said it is working on bank overdraft lines because of working capital pressure from payment cycles. Much of the quarter's growth came from a few large government and MICE programmes, and several answers were vague or deferred.

+437% YoY vs INR1.66 crore; QoQ up from INR3.81 crore
+307% YoY vs INR1.52 crore; QoQ up from INR1.8 crore
Management described company as debt free

segments.name: MICE (core)
segments.commentary: Management estimated MICE at about INR100 crore of Q1 revenue in one answer, then said INR50-60 crore in another, so the split is unclear. Oceania programmes worth about INR32 crore were completed, covering 950-1,000 delegates.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026 with more than 100 corporate clients signed; management put it at about 10-15% of revenue. Billing cycles run 1st-15th payable on the 20th and 16th-30th payable on the 6th-7th of the next month.

segments.name: Government and institutional (Punjab Yatra)
segments.commentary: Punjab Yatra contract worth about INR92 crore covering 1.85 lakh yatris, at about INR4,950 per person for a 2-night, 3-day trip. Management said about 15% of Q1 revenue came from it; about 1.15 lakh travelled to date and the contract runs to about November.

segments.name: IRCTC
segments.commentary: Empanelled as one of four or five A-listed vendors, with a first order of about INR75 lakh to INR1 crore. Empanelment term was stated as two years, extendable, but the executive director was not certain.

segments.name: B2B and B2C OTA / leisure
segments.commentary: B2B tool lets smaller travel agents book tickets. B2C app Machtravel.com is in testing and its launch was pushed from late August to September 2026. Leisure was described as doing very well, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around INR500-plus crore, reiterated and described as an average-based figure; management expects to surpass it.
Management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial because October-December is a festival and Christmas lull for corporate travel; Q2 is seasonally heavier than Q1 overall.
Management would not commit to a date for EBITDA margins returning to the roughly 10% level mentioned by an analyst, and would not say margins will be under pressure in Q2.
Markups may be compressed in aggressive pursuit of business, but management said the company will not burn money.
Next milestones named: INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue, B2C app launch in September, a possible main board move within 12 months, and new southern offices.
capex_capacity: Operating presence expanded to Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar and Ahmedabad; more southern offices planned.
Investment in technology, talent and offices over the past year is cited as the cause of lower margins; no quantified capex figure was given.
Corporate self-booking tool (SBT) covers booking, approval, ticketing, invoicing and reporting; management said it uses the same technology as large players.
Captive audience of about 1.25 lakh travellers a year is to be moved onto the B2C portal and app.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the growth to the transition beyond MICE into corporate, B2B, leisure, government and B2C, and said the policies were implemented from 1 April 2026.
TTV (total ticketed volume) was about INR259-260 crore versus about INR143 crore in revenue; the call did not reconcile TTV with GMV of INR252 crore.
Management said pricing on the B2C app is at par with large B2C players.
Punjab Yatra daily flows are about 1,100 travellers out and 1,100 back, with about 3,300-3,500 people handled at any one time.
Management said it is not clear whether the Punjab yatra will be repeated; three other Punjab yatra programmes were not won. Management is in talks with other state governments.

qa_highlights.question: How did revenue grow from INR22 crore to INR140-plus crore, and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company spent about 1.5 years building new teams and technology and implemented the policies from April 2026. Revenue now comes from MICE, corporate, leisure, government and B2B; TTV was about INR259-260 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be managed to support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt free with about INR3 crore of debt, but payment-cycle issues have created a working capital need. It is working toward bank overdraft facilities and will update the market if availed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between core MICE and the new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was unsure of the exact split. It said about INR50-60 crore came from MICE in one answer and about INR100 crore in another, with corporate at 10-15% and the Punjab Yatra at about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margins recover to about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no firm date. It said margins will improve as business scales, buying power rises and markups increase, but that it will be aggressive in the market and may give up some markup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore guidance conservative given Q1 was about 29-30% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is an annual average and cited seasonality. It said it hopes to surpass INR500 crore, but expects no substantial quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 and Q3 because of festival periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Yatra contract repeatable, and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is for 1.85 lakh yatris at about INR4,950 per person and runs to about November. Payment is about 7 days after travel, roughly 15 days in total. It was unsure whether the programme would be repeated.

risks_watch: Working capital strain: management said payment cycles have created a working capital need and the company is working toward bank overdraft lines; watch for the OD sanction, size and terms.

Margin trajectory: EBITDA margin was 6.09% vs 7.17% a year ago, and management gave no date for recovery and said it will give up some markup to win business.
Unclear revenue split: management gave MICE as INR50-60 crore in one answer and about INR100 crore in another; TTV of about INR259-260 crore was not reconciled with GMV of about INR252 crore.

Q2 and Q3 guidance: management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial due to festival and Christmas seasonality; watch Q2 numbers against the INR500-plus crore FY27 target and the B2C app launch slipping to September 2026.

544252|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% to INR669 crore (20% ex one-time tax benefit), with AUM up 23% and GNPA steady at 27 bps.
544252|2026-03.overview: AUM crossed INR140,000 crore, growing 23% YoY, with quarterly AUM additions of INR7,294 crore and disbursements up 23% YoY to INR17,506 crore. Spreads compressed 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and NIM fell 12 bps to 3.8% on lower acquisition yields and a 15 bps PLR pass-through in December. Asset quality held (GNPA 27 bps, NNPA 11 bps), but annualised credit cost rose to 19 bps from 11 bps YoY on a deliberate Stage 2 provision top-up. Management guided to ROA compression of about 10 bps in FY27 (towards upper end of the 2.0-2.2% medium-term range) assuming no policy rate change, and said it will firm up guidance with Q1 results.

segments.commentary: AUM grew 24% YoY, 10.8% of mix, up 10 bps QoQ. LAP GNPA fell 6 bps to 46 bps; on-book yield about 150 bps above home loans.

segments.name: Lease rental discounting (LRD)
segments.commentary: AUM grew 44% YoY, 22.4% of mix, up 50 bps QoQ. Nil GNPA; yield about 7.9-8.0%, lower-margin product.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF) / construction finance
segments.commentary: DF AUM grew 13% YoY (11.5% mix) as funded projects generate higher cash flows. Highest-margin product; yield about 11.5-11.75%. Construction finance GNPA flat at 3 bps.

segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursements of INR410-425 crore in Q4, targeting INR600 crore+ within 12 months. AUM about INR9,000 crore (mix roughly 70:30 affordable to near prime); ATS INR28 lakh, 68% salaried, about 65% with CIBIL above 750. Operates in 73 locations.

BT-out rate unchanged from Q3 at about 10% of AUM (total attrition about 20%); largest BT-out destination is public sector banks. Management expects BT-out to decline from May if rates stay stable.
Industry IHL growth about 9.5% per latest data; company targets 21-23% growth.
Acquisition yields fell in Q4; portfolio yield down 14 bps QoQ from lower acquisition pricing and attrition of higher-rate book.
Bounce metrics (first bounce, early bounce, 12-month bounce) reportedly improving QoQ through March; April bounce trends described as same.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall 12 bps and what is the outlook for Q1 yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower acquisition pricing and the full impact of the 15 bps PLR pass-through from December drove the decline. Q1 yields expected broadly sideways with slight compression; cost of funds to fall 3-5 bps in Q1 per the CFO, later framed as 2-3 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA likely to stay above the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 ROA should be at the upper end of the 2.0-2.2% range, with about 10 bps compression from NIM pressure; leverage lifts ROE but not ROA. Full guidance to follow with Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut PLR further?
qa_highlights.answer: No further PLR cut envisaged absent a repo change; money market rates are elevated, with OIS pricing about 75 bps of hikes, which management says it does not fully believe.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Stage 2 coverage raised and are early bounce trends deteriorating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bounce metrics are improving QoQ across segments and April is the same; the Stage 2 coverage increase was a prudential top-up given the macro environment, with no micro stress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sambhav AUM and its near-prime/affordable mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Sambhav AUM is close to INR9,000 crore, roughly 70:30 between affordable and near prime; exact split to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Will fee and assignment income keep growing faster than loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose to INR297 crore from INR200 crore, driven by insurance and foreclosure income. Assignment income is a balancing lever and fee income is expected to grow in line with the business.

544252|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Housing Q1 FY27: record AUM addition of INR8,918 crore (AUM up 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore) and PAT up 23% to INR715 crore, but NIM fell 14 bps to 3.7%.
544252|2026-06.overview: Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR19,509 crore, a record quarter, and AUM grew 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore. PAT grew 23% YoY to INR715 crore, with ROA stable at 2.3% and ROE up to 12.5%. Net margin compressed 14 bps QoQ to 3.7% as portfolio yield fell, while cost of funds eased 7 bps to 7.2%. Q1 credit cost of 5 bps was flattered by a one-off assignment of about INR2,300 crore, and management guided FY27 NIM down 20-25 bps and credit cost at 10-15 bps.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: Growth improved to 20% YoY; 54.1% of AUM. GNPA moderated 1 bp QoQ to 34 bps. Balance-transfer-out pressure eased slightly in Q1, to be watched for one more quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew 22% YoY; 10.3% of AUM, down 50 bps QoQ in mix. GNPA rose to 62 bps from 46 bps on one-week account movement; management cites a 50-70 bps historical corridor.

segments.name: Lease rental discounting (LRD)
segments.commentary: Grew 41% YoY; 23.1% of AUM, up 70 bps QoQ in mix, the fastest-growing product.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% YoY; 11.4% of AUM, down 10 bps QoQ. GNPA at 12 bps after one account moved from Stage 2 to Stage 3.

segments.name: Sambhav Housing (affordable and near-prime)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate INR450-465 crore vs INR410-425 crore in Q4. Operational in 73 urban and 72 rural locations; target INR600 crore+ monthly in the next 9 months. About 65% of customers have bureau score above 750, and salaried mix is 68%.

Cost of funds sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias.

Fee and commission income growth is linked to disbursement growth through insurance income and foreclosure, bounce and penal charges.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

Sambhav ticket size and Tier 2/3 expansion may dilute average ticket size and yield; the affordable segment is ramping.

rows.label: Acquisition pricing in prime housing stable; no upward move assumed
rows.why: Management does not expect large-scale pricing moves and has not factored them in, while prime attrition at higher historical yields keeps pushing portfolio yield lower (portfolio yield 8.9%, compressed QoQ).

rows.label: Cost of funds sideways with downward bias in Q2

rows.label: Sambhav ticket size drift lower

544252|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 FY27: PAT up 18% YoY to INR757 crore, AUM at INR1.58 lakh crore growing 25%, with management flagging ~25 bps NIM compression ahead.
544252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed AUM crossing INR1.5 lakh crore, disbursements up 25% YoY to INR19,900 crore, and stable asset quality (GNPA 29 bps, NNPA 12 bps). Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: AUM growth 22% YoY (vs 20% in Q1); home loans are 53.9% of AUM. GNPA 36 bps (up from 34 bps); NNPA 16 bps (up 1 bp).

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM growth 26% YoY. GNPA down 1 bp QoQ to 61 bps; NNPA down 4 bps to 21 bps.

segments.name: Loan against rental/LRD
segments.commentary: AUM growth 39% YoY (vs 41% in Q1). GNPA 2 bps, due to one retail account moving from Stage 2 to NPA; NNPA 1 bp. Management says excluding this, quality remains strong.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF)
segments.commentary: AUM growth 13% YoY and the book declined QoQ on higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements. GNPA flat at 12 bps; NNPA down 3 bps. Management targets 15-17% of portfolio.

segments.name: Sambhav (affordable housing)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate crossed INR500 crore; now 16% of home loan originations by value (vs 14% in Q1). ATS about INR28 lakh; 65% of customers have bureau score above 750; 66% salaried.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 21-23% for FY27 kept unchanged; AUM is currently growing 25%, but management flagged a possible slowdown to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags the repo hike.
NIM compression of about 25 bps for the year reiterated; management said a further 1-2 bps hit is possible if acquisition pricing pressure is severe.
ROA guidance of 2.1-2.3% retained; current 2.2%, with possibly 2-3 bps of additional compression in a stress case.
Management expects the repo hike to flow through about 80-82% to cost of funds and portfolio yields. Under a 75 bps hike scenario, cost of funds could rise about 61-62 bps to exit FY27.
Sambhav targeted at about 20% of home loan mix by year-end and around 30% over 3-4 years; monthly disbursement target of INR600 crore by year-end.
Opex to NTI, targeted to fall about 1% a year, may stay flat next year if insurance commission cuts are implemented. Salary costs to keep rising YoY for about four more quarters.
capex_capacity: Network at 223 branches across 182 locations.
Sambhav runs a centralised underwriting model with regionalised operations centres, and is scaling via B2C, B2B and D2C channels.
Management is recalibrating the mix toward non-prime, LAP and construction finance if prime acquisition pricing stays weak.
demand_pricing: Portfolio yield fell to 8.8%; incremental loan yield around 8.1% in both Q1 and Q2. Management expects pass-through of the repo hike to the portfolio in line with cost of funds.

Floating-rate assets: 25-30% linked to repo; internal FRR book (about 54% of assets, or 60-62% of floating assets) linked to PLR. PLR raised 15 bps effective 16 October 2026; new acquisition pricing expected to rise about 15-20 bps.
Bank MCLR hikes by leading public sector banks and an early 15-20 bps move by one or two banks were cited; a clearer picture expected around 24-25 October.
Management said prime pricing competition from PSU and private banks is an ongoing feature; if acquisition pricing lags, prime attrition may rise and the company will lean on non-prime growth.

Insurance commission regulation draft: management estimated 10-11% of PBT comes from cross-sell income; about 4-5% can be offset, leaving 6-7% of PBT at risk. Sambhav fees and prime efficiencies may offset part of this, mainly on a longer-term basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

risks_watch: Acquisition pricing pass-through by banks after the repo hike, due around 24-25 October; a lag could increase prime attrition and cut AUM growth from 25% toward 22-23%.
Insurance commission regulation: a 6-7% PBT impact is possible if the draft guidelines stand, which would push opex to NTI flat next year.
Developer finance book: a QoQ decline and 13% YoY growth; watch whether disbursements recover in Q3-Q4 as management expects.
Rising salary costs (19% YoY in Q2) as Sambhav and senior hires build out; management expects elevated costs for 1.5-2 years.
Home loan GNPA rose to 36 bps from 34 bps; watch for further upward movement, and whether the single LRD slippage stays isolated.
544252|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and profitability. Cautious and non-committal on margins and acquisition pricing, which management said is still unclear after the repo hike, and it declined to revise guidance.
key_quotes: Overall good quarter across growth, asset quality, and profitability.

We are yet to see the impact in the market because acquisition pricing not moving can lead to a higher attrition pressure again largely on the prime housing and some extent LRD, because both of these are most price-sensitive customers.
So, largely we are an optimized balance sheet with interest rate having asset to liability floating almost completely matched.

544253|2026-03.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.
544253|2026-03.overview: Kross closed FY26 with revenue of INR 673.2 crore (+8.5%) and PAT of INR 55.2 crore (8.2% margin), after a slow H1 and a stronger H2 (H2 revenue 49.2% above H1). Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA growth stated as 8.2% (transcript reads 87.9%, likely a transcription error)

financial_highlights.value: Trailer axles and suspension 43%; other components 57%

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspension
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes were over 10,500 trailer axles and over 3,500 suspension units, with air and mechanical suspension leading the pick-up. Q4 mix was about 60% suspension and 40% axles, and FY26 axle to suspension mix was about 70:30.

segments.name: Tipping Jacks (new)
segments.commentary: Launched and validated in Q4 FY26, with 75-80 kits sold in Q4 and 150-200 kits guided for Q1 FY27. Management targets 300 units by end-Q1 and 500 units each in Q2 and Q3, and says revenue will pick up at 300-400 kits a month.

segments.name: Tractor and Agri
segments.commentary: Tractor is about 9% of revenue, with a target of about 15% within two years. A third large tractor OEM is to start revenue from Q1 FY27, alongside diversification with existing two OEMs into forgings, shafts and castings.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of FY26 revenue. Management cites secured orders from European Tier-1 customers and aims to raise the share over two years; export of extruded axles will wait until the line runs above 5,000 beams a month.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of about 22% (Q4 rate) to continue in FY27, subject to demand; 45 days into Q1, trends were described as robust.
Gross margin / EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for coming quarters; Q1 FY27 may see one to two points of pressure as commodity pass-through is retrospective by about one quarter.
Seamless tube plant expected to be commissioned by end-FY27 (Q4 FY27); its revenue contribution starts in FY28, after in-house consumption.
OEMs are targeting high single-digit volume growth for FY27 across CV segments, per management.
Capex guided at about INR 100 crore for seamless tube and INR 20-25 crore for other business in FY27, plus maintenance capex. About INR 60 crore was spent on seamless tube in FY26.
capex_capacity: Extruded axle beam line commissioned; trials are complete and axle sales are expected from late May or June 2026. Management says the line is producing or targeting upward of 5,000 axle beams a month, versus earlier stated capacity of 5,000 axles a month expanding to 7,500 with the new plant.
Seamless tube facility: construction almost complete. Piercer to be dispatched from China by end-May 2026; rotary hearth furnace from Wesman is being installed.
High Pressure Mold Line to be operational by September 2026, doubling casting capacity. Another casting line planned for September-October 2026.
New robotic forging facility for rear axle shafts to be ready for supply by September 2026. Multiple high-tonnage forging presses already commissioned.
Forging and machining expansion described as mostly complete; furnace fuel switched away from sole LPG dependence.
demand_pricing: Management says M&HCV demand is strong: Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland reported strong Q4 volume growth that continued in April 2026. Production runs above 10,000-12,000 trucks a month across the two largest CV OEMs, below the Feb-Mar peak of 14,000-15,000.
Price hike of about 5% taken in trailer axles and suspension, which the company says is in line with competitor moves of about 4%. Management says it cannot price above the #1 player.

Steel price increase of INR 3-5/kg being negotiated with OEMs from April 2026. Conversion cost increase requested for tooling, oils and gas. OEM pass-through is retrospective but delayed by about one quarter; axle and suspension business has no retrospective recovery.
Steel mills are holding about 50-60% of ordered stock, so supply is tight but available. LPG shortage led to furnace fuel changes.
Management says rail freight corridor will affect only a small portion of trailer demand, mainly rigid-body vehicles.
Demand from fabricators for extruded axles is strong, but the company cannot meet it yet due to ramp-up constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the tractor target of about 15% of revenue, given single-digit tractor industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites new customer addition (third large tractor OEM starting Q1) and new products (forgings, shafts, castings) with the two existing OEMs, with the target over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 22% Q4 growth sustainable, and what are volume trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is planning for that pace if the last six months' tonnage and demand trends hold. Q1 FY27 is seen as better than Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected commodity and margin impact in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel hike of INR 3-5/kg is effective April but retrospective recovery is delayed about one quarter, so Q1 margin pressure is expected. Management guides 14-15% margin for later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the seamless tube capex and when does revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 60 crore was spent in FY26, with about INR 100 crore planned for FY27. Plant commissioning is expected around Q4 FY27 and revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rail freight corridor affect trailer demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact will be limited to a small portion of trailer demand and would mainly affect rigid-body vehicles.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from steel and consumable cost increases before OEM settlement, with the retrospective recovery delayed about one quarter.
Fuel-price and LPG shortage effects on CV operator demand and on the company's furnace-based heat treatment.
Ramp-up of the extruded axle line to the 5,000+ beams/month level, and the Tipping Jacks targets of 300/500 units per quarter.
Seamless tube commissioning slippage beyond Q4 FY27; seamless revenue is not expected until FY28.
Tractor target of about 15% revenue within two years depends on the third OEM's ramp-up and new product wins.
Q2 monsoon seasonality in CV demand. Management noted weaker Q2 seasonality.
Note the transcript contains an apparent error in the FY26 EBITDA growth figure ('87.9%'), and the Q4 PAT margin ('69 bps') and the Q4 EBITDA margin of 14.9% need checking against filings.

So, it is not going to be in this financial year that the seamless tube will contribute towards revenue growth.

544253|2026-06.headline: Kross Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32.3% YoY to INR184.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.23% (up 63 bps) and PAT up 24.4% to INR133.12 million.
544253|2026-06.overview: Kross reported its best-ever Q1 top line, with revenue of INR184.3 crore (up 32.3% YoY) and EBITDA up 39.5% YoY to INR225.54 million. Management attributed growth to volumes across M&HCV, trailers and tractors, and said the extrusion axle beam line is now in production. Steel and conversion-cost pass-throughs are being settled, with the tractor industry already settled from April 1 and CV settlement pending. Management said Q1 is in line with its FY27 targets, though June-July demand is seasonally subdued.

financial_highlights.change: +32.3% YoY vs INR139.3 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue mix: trailers, axles, suspensions and tipping

financial_highlights.change: Management targets 40-45% export growth this FY

segments.name: M&HCV / CV
segments.commentary: Momentum from Q4 FY26 continued into Q1; OEMs indicate a strong September quarter and stronger Q3 and Q4, backed by order books. Tractor-trailer and tipper segments expected to grow well.

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspensions
segments.commentary: Q1 axle volume about 9,500 numbers and suspension volume about 3,200-3,300 (mechanical and air). Volumes up about 30% YoY; management attributes this to Q4 FY26 order spillover and capacity that capped Q4 sales.

segments.name: Tipping jacks
segments.commentary: About 200 kits (management also cited 226 sold in Q1) against 800 per month capacity; management expects 65-70% utilisation by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Tractor
segments.commentary: Demand described as consistent; management expects the tractor contribution to rise meaningfully over coming years.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Existing supply to a European tier 1 is on plan. Four to five product lines are in play; one is in mass production and three are scheduled from H2 FY27. Target of about 8% export share in two years, from about 4-4.5% now.

544253|2026-09.headline: Kross Q2 FY27 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR235 crore with EBITDA margin of 13%, but reported PAT was a loss of INR19.7 million.

H1 FY27 revenue was INR419 crore versus INR270 crore a year earlier, with H1 EBITDA of INR53 crore. Management attributed growth to trailer and CV demand after monsoons, share gains with larger customers, and exports; margins were pressured by steel and consumable cost inflation, with price compensation expected in Q3 and Q4. The seamless tube backward-integration project (budget ~INR170 crore) is progressing, with production trials targeted for Feb-March 2027 (or end Q4 per another answer).

segments.commentary: Contributed ~51% of Q2 revenue. Exports ~7.5-8% of component business, with management targeting ~45% export growth YoY this year. Tipping jacks: capacity ~800 units, 50-60% utilisation targeted by Q4; realisation ~INR1.4 lakh per set.

demand_pricing: CV demand strong since GST rationalisation; monsoon-related deferment ended around July, with demand picking up in August per management.
Chhattisgarh market recovered after a long gap, contributing to trailer order growth; share gains with larger customers cited.
Q2 tractor volumes linked to TAFE planned production of 13,000-14,000 tractors in October; below-average rainfall noted by analyst.
Competition in trailer axles: York (market leader), Tata Motors, BPW and Hendrickson; components face product-family-specific competitors.

Rising steel and consumable costs compressed Q2 gross margin versus Q1 despite some price escalation; management says settlements with most OEMs/Tier 1s are underway with retrospective compensation expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove growth above the industry for trailer axles and component segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-monsoon demand pickup from August, share gains with larger customers, new regional demand (e.g. Chhattisgarh), and export growth (~7.5-8% of component business).

qa_highlights.question: Volume and value growth for axles and suspensions in Q2 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 trailer axles above 10,500 and H1 nearly 20,000, up about 50-55% YoY; trailer value ~INR115 crore in Q2 vs ~INR58-60 crore a year earlier. Suspension volume not disclosed; to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt rise by end FY27?

Management expects retrospective compensation but declined to give a timeline for returning to 14-15% EBITDA margin.

544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

segments.name: Retreading materials (tread rubber, PCTR)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of sales come from tread rubber; retread margins were hit by the GST mismatch (18% on retread materials vs 5% on new agricultural tyres), and dealer off-take fell. Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.name: Tyres (incl. agricultural, two-wheeler, tractor rear)
segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.name: UAE operations (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: management expects to at least maintain FY26 levels of performance, and will review this after Q2 FY27 depending on how the situation evolves.
Management expects West Asia and India-related disruptions to normalise by end of Q2 FY27 (pricing, raw material and shipping), which would support better Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.
Management expects a Terra Rubber recycling-linked margin benefit in FY26/FY27 through in-house offtake; no quantified synergy was given.
Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.
capex_capacity: Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; the plant has been operating for about 10 years.
Indian utilisation is about 45-55%: retread segment about 55% and tyre segment about 45%.
Gujarat depot commenced operations on December 1, 2025, serving tyre and retread products in Western India.
No significant capex is planned for FY27, as existing capacity is sufficient; cost reduction is focused on automation and AI-based planning tools.
Terra Rubber has started manufacturing and processing scrap into products trialled on road; management is scouting acquisitions but nothing is finalised and no numbers were shared.
demand_pricing: Tyre production volume grew 36% YoY in FY26 (5,35,870 vs 3,93,253 units) and PCTR grew about 10%; bonding gum and flaps grew 56%.
The GST cut on new commercial and agricultural tyres (from 28% to 18% and 5%, respectively) left retread materials at 18%, which narrowed retreading's 30-40% price advantage to about 20%.
Q4 tyre volumes fell QoQ due to dealer off-take hesitancy amid war-related uncertainty in March 2026.
Dealer credit was extended by about one month to 4-5 months, with a stated plan to revert to 3-4 months; China dumping in GCC is extending credit terms up to a year.
Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher tyre production volumes, precured tyres (Europe and the US, where repeat orders are starting), and Terra Rubber integration for in-house raw material offtake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

544256|2026-03.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.
544256|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR10,739 crore, with full-year gross margin up 280 bps to 12% and EBITDA margin up 180 bps to 6.6%. Q4 revenue grew 123% YoY to INR3,544 crore, but gross margin fell to 9.7% (about 230 bps down YoY) as gold bars and coins rose to 40% of sales, plus one-time discounts and franchise mix. Management attributes the Q4 margin dip to mix and one-offs, and it guided FY27 revenue of INR13,500 crore, EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%, with a review next quarter given the import duty hike.

segments.commentary: FY26 franchise revenue INR1,292 crore (+83% YoY); Q4 INR430 crore (+132% YoY). Franchise gross margin cited at 2.5-3%.

Management says the import duty and the advance authorisation scheme do not apply to its domestic business; the duty is passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

risks_watch: Q4 gross margin at 9.7% versus 12-13% guidance; management says the mix shift will normalise, but its explanation of one-offs has been challenged.
Import duty hike may reduce bars and coins demand (20-22% of sales); whether jewellery exchange offsets it is unproven, and management said it is too early to quantify FY27 volume.
Hedging at 67% is short of the 75-80% target; MCX margin costs and unhedged gains affect margin volatility.
Franchise mix rising (FOCO margins about 2-3%) could weigh on gross margin as the network expands.
Inventory turnover fell to 3.8x as new stores ramp; the new-market ramp needs watching.
Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027; the QIP enabling resolution lapses end-August 2026.
544256|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the full-year result and the FY27 guidance, but defensive on Q4 margins: management repeatedly ties the drop to bars and coins and one-off promotions and says it is not structural. It was less specific on FY27 volume, the QIP and hedging costs, and said it would update guidance next quarter.
key_quotes: So, the three factors primarily which can identify to this are higher share of gold bars and coins in the overall sales mix.
We therefore view the gross margin impact as largely one-time and mix-driven, not structural, and remain focused on improving product mix and margins as our stores mature.
So, we feel looking at these positives, you know, we feel that INR12,500 can be stretched to INR13,500, and that's where the guidance is coming from.
The business is self-sufficient.

rows.label: Franchise mix drag on gross margin

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.
544256|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, driven by retail (up 56%, with 46% SSSG), franchise (up 8%) and e-commerce (up 20%). EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

financial_highlights.change: Reported gross margin flat YoY; adjusted ex-hedging up ~40-50 bps per CFO
vs ~INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst cited INR31 crore, CFO disputed); lower FD balances on mortgage

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 56% with 46% SSSG; now about 78% of total revenue, with jewellery about 78-79% of retail and bars/coins about 20-21%. Newer North and Central India stores run 15-18% studded ratios.

segments.name: Franchise
segments.commentary: Grew 8% YoY; management attributed the slowdown to B2B billing timing and stock replenishment, with franchise openings expected to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle planned).

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 20% YoY; company is deliberately shifting mix towards jewellery and away from bars/coins, so management expects better margins but slower total sales growth.

segments.name: Litestyle by PNG
segments.commentary: Studded ratio 32.9% in Q1; current litestyle gross margin of about 18-20%, with management targeting about 50% studded ratio in two years and 30-35% margin later.

guidance_outlook: Open around 25 stores in FY27, taking network to about 103 by March 2027 (63 COCO, balance FOCO); a few launches in Q2, bulk in Q3-Q4.
Network targets: about 140 stores by March 2028 and about 177 by March 2029 (about 113 legacy and 64 litestyle; about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO by March 2029).
EBITDA margin guidance of about 7% for full year FY27; other expenses about 3% of sales or roughly INR400 crore for FY27.
PAT margin underlying (ex-hedging gains) targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per CFO, versus 4.2% per CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29.
Hedging coverage to reach about 80% around Q3 FY27 (Q2 around 80% per CEO), and fully hedged in FY28; currently 70%+.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to be reduced by INR500-600 crore by FY29, non-GML borrowing about INR1,200 crore; targeted debt-free in four to five years.
Gross margin guidance for retail mix of 13-14% (CFO: 12.5-13.5% at 10-11% studded ratio), including hedging gains shown separately.
capex_capacity: Store count 78 at end-Q1 FY27 (57 COCO, 21 FOCO).
FY27 plan: 25 new stores, bulk in Q3 and Q4, franchise-led; deepening Maharashtra and expanding UP, Bihar, Central India and NCR.
UP stores running 18%+ studded versus 15% projection; 8-10 UP franchise openings planned in FY27; Ayodhya store opening soon.
Capital allocation focused on store expansion, franchise network, digital and operational excellence, funded from internal accruals.
Management plans a QIP at a suitable time to reduce promoter holding (above 75%); board enabling resolution already in place.
demand_pricing: Management said demand held up through April-June despite record gold prices, supported by weddings and Akshaya Tritiya; Adhik Maas was muted due to high silver prices.
Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and a large part of Q3.
Customers shifting towards lightweight jewellery, studded products and old gold exchange, favouring organised players.
Hedging gains: Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore, Q2 FY26 about INR5.5-6 crore; gains shrinking as hedging coverage rises.
Marketing kept within 1.5% of sales; 250-300 hoardings cut versus last year. FY26 other expenses included about INR40-50 crore for UP launch and one-time campaigns that are not expected to recur.
Inventory turns stabilised at about 3.5-4x after refinery and B2B sales wound down (previously about 7x).

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin flat YoY despite mix shift toward retail, and what is the ideal retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported gross margin is flat because hedging gains are shown separately; ex-hedging adjusted gross margin is up about 40-50 bps YoY. Management targets 12.5-13.5% retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio, and 13-14% overall retail gross margin including hedging gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conservative spending amid demand uncertainty, lower scheme-redemption discounts, marketing kept within 1.5% of sales with 250-300 hoardings cut, and no store launches in Q1. Spending will rise in Q3-Q4 with expansion, but EBITDA guidance is still expected to be met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 other expense guidance and why was other income so different between Q4 and Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses are guided at about 3% of sales, roughly INR400 crore for FY27. Other income was about INR10 crore in Q1 versus about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, who said lower fixed deposits placed on mortgage drove the decline; cash and hedging margin money also hold some balances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion and COCO/FOCO mix plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan adds 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), then 37 each in FY28 and FY29 to reach 140 and 177. By March 2029, about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO, with 113 legacy and 64 litestyle stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and hedging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin underlying ex-hedging is targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per the CFO, versus about 4.2% per the CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29. Hedging is about 70%+ now, targeted at about 80% around Q3 FY27 and fully hedged in FY28. Hedging gains were about INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR5.5-6 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is Litestyle progressing on studded mix, gross margin and store count?
qa_highlights.answer: Studded ratio is about 32.9-34% now, targeted at about 50% in a couple of years. Current litestyle gross margin is about 18-20%, versus 30-35% for the format once studded mix rises. Litestyle store target is 65-70 by March 2029 and about 100 over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why are franchise revenue growth (8%) and e-commerce growth lower than company-operated stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise sales are booked as B2B, so initial stocking and replenishment timing affect quarterly numbers; management expects franchise openings to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle). E-commerce is deliberately shifting mix away from bars and coins toward jewellery, so margins should improve but total sales growth may slow.

risks_watch: Reported gross margin flat YoY; expansion of hedging gains is shrinking as hedging coverage rises toward 80% by Q3 FY27 and full coverage in FY28, so reported margin depends on underlying retail mix.
Other expenses are guided to rise in Q3-Q4 with store openings; Q1 spend (about 5% growth) was unusually low, so H2 cost run-rate against about INR400 crore guidance needs monitoring.
Franchise revenue growth of 8% versus company-operated retail growth of 56%; visibility into franchise B2C sell-through is still being built and management has only recently gained system access.
Promoter holding above 75% with a QIP planned at a suitable time; timing and size are not specified and the stock overhang remains.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to fall by INR500-600 crore by FY29; execution of the debt-reduction path and the litestyle studded-mix shift (from about 34% toward 50%) are key checkpoints.

Other income fell to about INR10 crore from about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, after the analyst cited INR31 crore; the figure was disputed on the call and should be reconciled against the filed numbers.
key_quotes: Their confidence has enabled us to deliver our highest ever first quarter, beginning FY27 on a strong note.
Despite elevated gold prices, our performa nce remains in line with our previously communicated guidance.
So franchise apple-to-apple on a quarter-to-quarter, these differences which will come, but having said that, we understand because franchise is our focus now, will be becoming big.
Eventually, we plan to take it to 80% studded inventory at a store le vel and 20% gold inventory and that would also enable us to reach a 50% to 60% studded ratio in that category.

Cautious and somewhat evasive on the reasons for flat gross margin and the other income gap, leaning on adjusted (ex-hedging) figures and deferring some answers to later quarters.

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

financial_highlights.change: +4% QoQ from INR478 crore in Q3
down from INR27 crore in Q3
down from INR10.8 crore in Q3; margin 1.7% vs 2.3%

financial_highlights.value: over INR70 crore (management cited INR74 crore in Q&A)

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 34,404 containers, down 10.96% QoQ and 3.17% YoY; FY26 volume 1,40,225, up about 5% YoY. Management says the company held up better than the industry, which saw about a 40% fall in March. Growth is shifting to East Coast ports.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

segments.name: Devaliya MMCT (Morbi)
segments.commentary: 32-acre multimodal terminal now fully operational. Tiles throughput fell sharply in March due to propane and natural gas shortages affecting about 700 units; volumes are rising month-on-month in industrial chemicals.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal numerical guidance. It expects EBITDA margin to recover from about 4.6-4.7% toward roughly 7%, which it says was the FY25 level.
Management expects sequential improvement in both top line and bottom line from Q1 FY27, and says it is comfortable with the trend in May.
Management targets debtor days below 120 in FY27.
FY27 capex planned at INR100 crore, of which INR92 crore is said to be funded from remaining IPO proceeds; spend is tied to customer orders and will be calibrated to EXIM normalisation.
Management expects operating cash flow to improve as realisations and EXIM volumes recover.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was over INR70 crore (about INR74 crore per Q&A), spent on specialised containers, reach stackers, commercial vehicles and handling equipment.
The company procured 161 specialised containers in FY26; a further order of similar size is under production and is expected to enter operations from the end of May 2026 over the next 1-1.5 quarters.
Own specialised container fleet is over 1,000 units.
Devaliya MMCT (32 acres, Morbi) is fully operational; fixed rail services run from Devaliya to CMLK, Bangalore, Chennai, Calcutta and Guwahati at lower frequency.
FY27 capex of INR100 crore covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles, reach stackers, forklifts and large cranes.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is strong, with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year, and that the East Coast EXIM pipeline is robust.
Domestic demand for specialised containers is strong, with similar orders in the pipeline for FY27.

Industry-wide, about 40-45k Indian containers were stranded at March end; freight rates, war-risk surcharges and insurance costs rose sharply, with war-risk surcharges nearly doubling ocean freight in some cases.
Capacity on US and Europe routes is about 30-35% of normal; Cape of Good Hope diversions add about 3,500 nautical miles and 10-15 days.
Realisations were hit by geopolitical factors and are expected to improve as EXIM volumes recover.

Receivables have risen, with the company citing growth in retail MMCT customers (up 25-30% YoY) who pay only when the next consignment ships. Management said the company had INR600+ crore in receivables, a figure raised by an analyst and not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects working capital needs as the new Devaliya MMCT became operational.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a revenue split between rail, road and water?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue, saying it operates as a consolidated multimodal logistics provider and that splitting would distort the picture.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will cash flow turn positive, given negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26 and a planned INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets debtor days below 120 this year, says INR100 crore of IPO funds is still unspent, and expects realisations and cash flow to improve as EXIM recovers. It said the EXIM trade should improve within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What further margin pressure is coming from April pricing, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numerical guidance, but said margins should improve sequentially, with EBITDA margin targeted back toward 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the INR100 crore capex go and what are the domestic growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment. Domestic growth is expected to come from the Morbi MMLP, tiles volumes once propane supply returns, and Western seaboard clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of the ROE/ROCE decline and the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ROE and ROCE to return to strong double-digit levels as margins recover from 4.6-4.7%, citing a debt position it considers under control.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed (traffic about 5% of pre-war levels); the timing of EXIM normalisation is uncertain.
Tiles and steel demand in Morbi depends on propane and gas supply; about 700 units are affected.
Rising receivables and negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26, with debt up to INR217 crore.

Watch the pace of FY27 capex against the INR100 crore plan and its funding.

544258|2026-06.headline: Western Carriers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR465 crores, with PAT of about INR9 crores and domestic TEUs up 37%.
544258|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR465 crores from INR416 crores, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores (4.1% margin) and PAT of about INR9 crores, up about 13% QoQ. Total container throughput of 58,261 TEUs beat Q4 FY26 (57,754) for the first time, driven by domestic volumes up 37% YoY while EXIM grew only 3.2%. Management attributed EXIM weakness to Middle East war-linked vessel disruption and freight rate spikes, and said working capital days fell from 120 to about 111 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. Analysts pressed on the lack of price pass-through, weak cash generation and receivables; management did not commit to a price hike.

544261|2026-09.headline: Arkade Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs. 145 crore with 24% EBITDA margin; pre-sales moderated to Rs. 151 crore amid no new launches.
544261|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs. 145 crore, with operating EBITDA of Rs. 35 crore (24% margin) and PAT of Rs. 25 crore (17.14% PAT margin). Management attributed the year-on-year revenue decline to a high base from four projects that started revenue recognition in the prior-year quarter after crossing 25% construction. Collections grew 22% YoY to Rs. 183 crore, but pre-sales were moderate at Rs. 151 crore, with H1 pre-sales of Rs. 306 crore. The company added four Western Mumbai redevelopment projects (about 11 acres, Rs. 5,000 crore GDV) and targets two launches worth Rs. 2,850 crore in Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Down YoY; management cited high prior-year base, change % not stated in call (analyst cited 45.1% decline)
EBITDA margin 24%; described as broadly stable QoQ by analyst
Improved vs previous quarter per management
Analyst cited 20% YoY decline; management said flat QoQ

segments.name: Residential development (Mumbai/MMR)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs. 145 crore and H1 Rs. 292 crore; recognition lagged after a high prior-year base from four projects crossing 25% construction. Arkade Eden (Malad West) handed over and Arkade Pearl Phase 1 (Vile Parle) received OC ahead of RERA timeline.

guidance_outlook: Two launches with combined GDV of about Rs. 2,850 crore targeted in Q3 FY27; analyst-cited Rs. 600 crore figure for two launches was not corrected by management in the call.
Pre-sales target of about Rs. 1,000 crore for FY27 referenced by analyst; management said it can stay positive on exceeding Rs. 1,000 crore, with launches driving upside.
Thane Greenfield (Rs. 2,000 crore GDV) targeted for Q4 FY27 launch, subject to CC and RERA approval; to launch tower-wise over two years.
Filmistan project (analyst cited about Rs. 4,000 crore GDV) expected to launch next financial year per management; GDV raised on better rate realisation.
Pipeline GDV of about Rs. 19,000 crore across 5.7 million sq ft; launches planned over next 4-5 years.
Revenue recognition expected to improve in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 from recently launched Arkade Evoke (Bangur Nagar) and Arkade Sapphire (Santacruz).
capex_capacity: Projects are about 60-70% complete; around 30% of remaining construction cost yet to be incurred, per CFO.
About Rs. 70 crore spent on approvals for upcoming projects (Satya Shripal, Nutan Ayojan/Ascend), carried in inventory.
Four Western Mumbai redevelopments (Malad, Kandivali, Borivali; about 11 acres, 15 lakh sq ft saleable carpet area, Rs. 5,000 crore GDV) at preferred-developer stage, DA process pending.
Yogi Nagar DA finalised between lawyers; requires society SGM approvals before registration.
Thane project: LOI received, CC awaited, MOE in place; five towers on six acres.
Bhandup Woollen Mills MOU expected to complete in the next few months; South Bombay redevelopment in bidding (top developers in 79A voting).
demand_pricing: Management attributed moderate pre-sales to no new launches so far; existing projects have healthy demand and Q2 pre-sales were flat QoQ.
Realisations improved on existing projects, lifting gross margin to 35%; OC receipt added natural appreciation per management.
Analyst said pre-sales fell about 20% YoY; management did not dispute and pointed to launch timing.
Competition in Mumbai redevelopment has increased sharply in the last 12-18 months, per management.
Company has about 15 completed redevelopment projects over 15-20 years and 5-6 ongoing; bids selectively on location, size and GDV.

qa_highlights.question: Why were pre-sales moderate in H1 and what is the outlook for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said moderation was company-specific because new launches were not yet out; Q2 pre-sales were flat QoQ and existing projects have healthy demand.

qa_highlights.question: What sales will the Q3 launches generate and how will they be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are planned against construction milestones over a 4-5 year project timeline, spread evenly across years; channel inquiries are good, with numbers to be released on launch.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons behind the reported delay at Arkade Rare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the delay, saying the RERA handover date was pre-poned from 28 December to 27 December.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company prepared to execute a large Filmistan project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has added manpower and onboarded architect, MEP, landscape consultants and execution contractors experienced in large projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will land acquisitions continue and is expansion limited to MMR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the Bhandup MOU, a couple of other opportunities within 12 months, and said focus remains MMR; Navi Mumbai and South/North Mumbai proposals are being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise to 35% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher realisations on existing projects and OC-driven appreciation at Arkade Eden and Arkade Pearl; management said construction cost increases are spread over 2-3 years, so impact is gradual.

risks_watch: Pre-sales run-rate of about Rs. 150 crore per quarter depends on the two Q3 launches; no new launches have been done in H1.
Revenue recognition gap: Q2 revenue down sharply YoY and recovery depends on Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 construction milestones.
Execution scale-up for Filmistan and multiple redevelopments; management said no major challenges currently.

Several projects (Yogi Nagar, Western Mumbai redevelopments, Thane RERA, Bhandup) pending approvals or DA registration; timelines not fully committed.

544262|2026-03.headline: Manba Finance Q4 FY26: PAT up 39% YoY to INR 11 crore; FY26 AUM INR 1,713 crore, up 29% YoY, with NIM at 13.63%.
544262|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 net interest income of INR 50 crore (up 34% YoY) and PAT of INR 11 crore (up 39% YoY). For FY26, NII rose 24% to INR 162 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR 45 crore, with ROE at 11.65% and ROA at 2.63%. Asset quality improved slightly QoQ, with gross Stage-3 at 3.33% and net at 2.46%, and the company raised its provision coverage. Management guided to 25-30% AUM growth, with new products (MSME LAP, used car, 3-Wheeler) and geographies (Karnataka, UP, MP) being added.

GNPA from 3.38% in Dec 2025; NNPA from 2.57%

segments.commentary: MFL business 91.84%, DA and BC 4.43%, co-lending 2.62%, and 1.11% in the remaining category.

segments.name: Geography

Around 900+ sales staff out of about 1,800 employees; customer base over 2.20 lakh live customers after adding about 28,500 in the quarter.
Expansion focus on UP (about 1% market share) and MP (about 3% market share).
demand_pricing: Disbursement growth about 16% YoY, driven by 2-Wheeler demand and dealer expansion; 2-Wheeler grew about 14% in April per management.
Used 2-Wheeler ticket INR 55-60k with first-year performance described as promising; new 2-Wheeler ticket INR 80-85k.
New geographies lent at 18-19% versus 21-22% in established markets to attract stronger borrowers.

EV 2-Wheeler about 7-8% of industry; company's EV exposure is similar, with 3-Wheeler EV about INR 40 crore of a roughly INR 50 crore 3-Wheeler book. Management says EV 2-Wheeler NPA is about 1% after 3.5 years.
Small business loan growth is being slowed because of tighter credit policy and a weak demand environment; it is under 5% of AUM.
TVS Motor all-India MOU has helped onboard about 70 TVS 3-Wheeler dealers in three months, with subvention and credit-loss support from TVS.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected 2-Wheeler vs other product mix and new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: 2-Wheeler share to fall to about 65% in three years from about 84% now; Karnataka starts in Q2 and UP and MP are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable AUM growth rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is 25-30% growth per year; AUM expected at INR 2,300-2,400 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provision coverage rise from 24% to 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is to strengthen the balance sheet against Stage-3 assets and possible calamities, given strong profitability. Credit loss was about 1.12-1.25% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Current incremental cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about 10.50%, down from about 11.25% a year earlier; PTC deal at about 9.75% and an SBI sanction of INR 100 crore at about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Early signs of stress from fuel prices and the vehicle book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not much so far: 100-125cc bikes, EMI INR 3,500-4,000, 20-25% down payment. Small business loans are seeing tighter policy and higher rejections.

qa_highlights.question: Equity fundraise timing and valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeted Q2 or Q3 FY27, now possibly Q3 or Q4; shares traded around INR 140-150 in February and the company may wait for INR 135-150.

3-Wheeler EV and used-vehicle collection risk; management called 3-Wheeler collection very challenging, and 3-Wheeler yields and losses need monitoring.
Dependence on 2-Wheeler (about 84.5% of AUM); the shift in mix is planned but not yet visible.
Equity fundraise timing and dilution risk, which may be deferred 3-4 months depending on market conditions.
New-geography collection build-out in UP, MP and Karnataka, where lower yields are being used to manage risk.

544262|2026-06.headline: Manba Finance Q1 FY27: NII up 36% YoY to INR42 crore, PAT up 36% to INR13 crore, AUM up 22% YoY to INR1,731 crore.
544262|2026-06.overview: Manba Finance reported Q1 FY27 NII of INR42 crore (+36% YoY) and PAT of INR13 crore (+36% YoY), with AUM of INR1,731 crore (+22% YoY) and disbursements of INR226 crore (+37% YoY). Asset quality was stated as stable, with GNPA at 3.41% and NNPA at 2.52%, and ECL provisions of INR25 crore against an IRAC requirement of INR7.57 crore. Management reiterated 35-40% AUM growth guidance for FY27, entered South India via Namma Loan (Sreesastha) in Karnataka, and launched LAP for MSMEs and battery replacement finance for e-3W. Capital adequacy stood at 24.40%, with management planning to raise INR100 crore of preference capital by September or October.

INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27

segments.commentary: Stage 1 assets INR1,619 crore (93.55%), Stage 2 INR53 crore (3.4%), gross Stage 3 INR59 crore (3.41%); Stage 2 reported lower QoQ.

qa_highlights.answer: LAP expected at 2-3% of AUM by FY27 end; ticket size INR8-20 lakh targeting shop-owning businessmen.

qa_highlights.question: Which products will reduce two-wheeler dependence?
qa_highlights.answer: Personal loans, top-up loans (after vintage maturity), used two-wheeler loans, three-wheeler loans via TVS all-India tie-up, and small business loans (~INR6-7 crore disbursed monthly) and MSME LAP.

qa_highlights.question: Technology: proprietary vs outsourced and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of tech is proprietary; personal loan software spend increasing this year; overall tech cost share expected to stay similar. No capex-to-revenue percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on profitability for coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly guidance but expects growth in line with history, AUM growth 35-40%, and similar PAT performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowing decline QoQ and what is the cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing reduced because of ~INR350 crore liquidity at March-end; higher cost in the quarter came from carrying extra liquidity. No forward cost trajectory given beyond NIM commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was QoQ AUM growth only ~1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality: run-down in April-June with few festivals; expects a large jump in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Namma Loan AUM targets and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore; breakeven in 9-12 months, possibly 6-7 months given early response; senior hire from TVS Motor and TVS Credit.

So definitely September and most importantly third quarter will have a big jump in the AUM.
