544262|2026-09.headline: Manba Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR14 crores, NII up 40% to INR52 crores, AUM up 21% to INR1,811 crores.
544262|2026-09.overview: Manba Finance reported Q2 FY27 net interest income of INR52 crores (up 40% YoY) and PAT of INR14 crores (up 20% YoY), with H1 NII of INR94 crores (up 39%) and H1 PAT of INR27 crores (up 28%). AUM reached INR1,811 crores at September 30, 2026, up 21% YoY, while GNPA improved to 2.96% and NNPA to 2.19%. Management said a rating upgrade to A minus stable from CARE and lower borrowing costs (average cost 10.14%) should support margins, and reiterated 30-35% AUM growth guidance for FY27 despite H1 growth of about 20%. The call was hosted by Antique Stock Broking and included mostly retail-investor questions.

segments.name: 2-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 83.10% of portfolio; main growth driver in the quarter, supported by dealer network expansion and new locations. Dealer base about 1,900-1,932 across 148 locations in 7 states.

segments.name: Top-up loans
segments.commentary: 5.70% of portfolio; secured against existing 2-wheeler customers, quoted IRR around 32%.

segments.name: 3-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 3% of portfolio. Battery replacement loan for EV 3-wheelers launched about 2 months ago, limited to own customers and to be tested for 18 months.

segments.name: Used vehicle loans
segments.commentary: 1.60% of portfolio; used 2-wheeler loans quoted at 27-28% IRR, with 100-plus dealers added in the last 6 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP / small business loans
segments.commentary: Small business loan IRR about 27-28%, average ticket INR5 lakh, NPAs 3-4%. MSME LAP disbursement at INR2-2.5 crores per month, targeted at INR5 crores per month by January.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: Unsecured, IRR similar to top-up (around 32%); being scaled cautiously through DSAs.

guidance_outlook: AUM and disbursement growth guidance for FY27 of 30-35%; management said H1 AUM growth was about 20% and H2 festive season should close the gap.
Management expects FY28 growth to continue but gave no numerical guidance.

Borrowing costs: about INR600 crores of high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; management expects about 25 bps overall impact in Q3-Q4 and a 50-75 bps reduction in cost of funds from the rating upgrade.
NIM concern raised by an analyst: prior guidance of 13-14% versus about 12.3% currently; management said NIM would not be hit by the RBI rate hike.
Capital from INR100 crore preferential issue expected by November 6, 2026; management expects capital to support growth for 4-6 quarters.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared for FY27 (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: INR100 crore preferential issue of equity and warrants; board approved in Q2, principal approval from NSE and BSE received, funds expected by November 6, 2026.

Operations in 148 locations across 7 states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Karnataka); about 16 offices added in the last year and 5-6 more small business loan branches planned this quarter.
Karnataka launched about 60 days before the call, with 100-plus dealers onboarded; Karnataka season expected in January.
Technology spend about INR2 crores per year with a 28-person tech team; disbursement turnaround cut from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeted same-day by end of year.
Employee base about 2,061, of which 1,100-plus in sales; 2.45 lakh+ live customers after adding about 32,330 in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler registrations about 53 lakh units in Q2, with August and September both record highs; September retail registrations up 32% YoY per FADA.
Management expects Diwali and Navratri season to lift H2 disbursements; said October alone added INR120 crores of new AUM after run-down.
Competition in 2-wheeler loans named as IDFC, L&T and regional players such as Berar; management claims about 15% market share in locations operating for 4+ years.
Bounce rate about 18-20%, with 7-8% of customers remaining in bounce across tenure, per management.
NTC (new-to-credit) customers about 40% of the book; LTV capped at 75% for them.

qa_highlights.question: Growth timeline for newer states (UP, MP, Rajasthan) given Gujarat and Maharashtra hold about half the dealer base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Maharashtra and Gujarat dealer tie-ups are largely complete; new dealer additions are coming from Rajasthan, UP, MP and Karnataka, with 100-plus dealers onboarded in Karnataka in the first 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How many quarters the INR100 crore raise will support growth, and FY27-28 growth guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Capital should support growth for 4-6 quarters; FY27 guidance is 30-35% growth, with H1 at about 20% and festive season in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30-35% AUM growth achievable given H1 AUM growth of about INR98 crores, and any El Nino impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said October added INR120 crores of AUM and similar is expected in November; MSME LAP and small business loans, 5-6 new branches and 10-12 live BC partners were cited as additional drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expenses up 28% YoY in Q2; drivers and cost optimisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 16 new offices in the last year, Karnataka expansion and seasonal sales hiring, and said YoY cost comparison is not a fair measure given the expansion; NIM, average cost and credit cost were said to be improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Further cost-of-funds reduction and NIM trajectory (guidance 13-14% vs 12.3% currently).
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores of old high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; overall impact of about 25 bps expected in Q3-Q4, and new borrowings are at lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Share of NTC borrowers and delinquency comparison; used vehicle and high-yield products.
qa_highlights.answer: NTC share about 40%; behaviour broadly similar to other customers except those with CIBIL above 750. Used 2-wheeler IRR 27-28%, top-up and personal loan IRR about 32%.

risks_watch: AUM growth of 30-35% requires roughly INR400-450 crores of H2 additions versus H1 growth of about 20%; festive-season delivery is key.
Rising RBI repo rate versus management's expectation of 50-75 bps cost-of-funds reduction from the rating upgrade.
NIM at about 12.3% versus prior 13-14% guidance.
Operating expense growth of 28% YoY in Q2 with ongoing branch expansion.
Concentration in 2-wheeler (83.10%) and unsecured personal loans being scaled up; EV battery replacement product is untested.
Completion of the INR100 crore preferential issue by November 6, 2026.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.

Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.

Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

rows.why: FY26 module production rose 77% to 12.6 GW and Q4 production hit 4.2 GW (+104% YoY), with cell utilisation assumed at 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW, though Q4 cell output was only 0.7 GW and C&I orders are deferred by ALMM-II timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already under way; ingot wafer FY28, BESS phase 2 FY28
rows.why: Waaree 2.0 capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over two years is committed, with the ingot wafer raised from INR5,100 crore to INR6,200 crore and a fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore enabled by the board, so the main announcements are already made.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA of INR6,617 crore beat the INR5,500-6,000 crore guide, but FY27 guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore is new and management flagged H1 FY27 as a transition with Q4 margin compression.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 operating margin fell about 590 bps QoQ to ~18.6%, cash conversion is ~27%, and export shipments are stuck, so H1 FY27 could miss the path to the INR7,000 crore low end while the 10 GW cell line is commissioned.

rows.label: Cell line transition M10R to G12R lifts output and realisation 10-12%
rows.why: Three module lines are already converted to G12R and five lines still on M10R TOPCon are due to convert over about one quarter, with management citing a 10-12% lift in output and realisation.

rows.label: Cash conversion normalises to 70-100%
rows.why: Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were held up by Middle East logistics delays, and management expects 70-100% at normalised inventory, but this is unquantified on timing.

rows.label: US FEOC rules driving new US orders
rows.why: US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, management says this is driving new US orders, and US capacity rises to 4.2 GW with the 2.6 GW addition, with IRA benefit of ~$0.07/Wp.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Waaree 2.0 story, FY26 results and FY27 EBITDA guidance, but defensive on the Q4 margin drop, ~27% cash conversion and the QoQ order-book decline; analysts pushed on margins, working capital and deferred BESS and ALMM-II answers.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).
Imported cell about USD0.04-0.045/W versus Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W; DCR market price about USD0.12-0.13/W.
US market had about six months of installation lull due to tariff uncertainty; management reports recent order and enquiry pickup, including data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion timeline for 10 GW cell and wafer and battery capacity over FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 28 GW modules, 15.4 GW cells, 4 GW inverters and 20 GVA transformers by FY27-end; FY28 to see about 16-18 GW modules and about 10 GW cell output. The 10 GW Indian cell facility adds from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did module gross margin fall, and what are the recovery levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower IRA realisation in Q1 because US dispatches came from OEM manufacturing; delayed non-DCR offtake; softer exports. Levers are DCR cell output, US local scaling, exports from August, and non-DCR offtake over the six-month window.

qa_highlights.question: How are US export and US local manufacturing margins structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports from India earn about USD0.04-0.05/W EBITDA. US local manufacturing nets about USD0.055-0.06/W after expenses, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W. Management guides total US local realisation and EBITDA at USD0.07-0.08/W, helped by a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower-cost import option for cells compared with domestic manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported cell is about USD0.04-0.045/W against Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W and DCR market price of USD0.12-0.13/W.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS volume and earnings outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5.15 GWh container line is live and order book is building. The 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27. FEOC-compliant cell realisations are about 25-30% above Chinese pricing, with non-FEOC at USD75-80/kWh versus Chinese USD50-55/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholders approved about INR10,000 crore of fundraising including equity. Management says FY27 EBITDA is broadly sufficient to fund the capex and it will wait for the right market window. Balance capex is about INR22,000 crore over three years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation and a lower IRA realisation mix in Q1; watch whether 18.2% operating EBITDA margin recovers toward the FY27 guidance band.
Second-half weighted order book and inventory build; utilisation of India modules around 50% annualised in Q1 versus a 70-75% target for Q3-Q4.
Timing of the 10 GW Indian cell commissioning (targeted by December) and ALMM-II extension window; the non-DCR offtake ramp is unconfirmed.
US export clearance delays and the start of US local line output from August; US IRA incentive monetisation timing.
Capex execution across INR31,500 crore programme and the glass capex decision, with an update promised in about one quarter.
Pending QIP and funding plan; BESS Make-in-India incentive is not yet announced.

544279|2026-03.headline: Godavari Biorefineries FY26 total income rose 6% to INR2,000 crore and EBITDA 15.8% to INR139 crore, with Q4 EBITDA of INR92 crore (16.2% margin).

Profit after tax was INR3.5 crore versus a loss in FY25. Q4 revenue from operations was INR564 crore, EBITDA INR92 crore (margin 16.2% versus 9.8% in Q3), and PAT INR52.9 crore versus INR8.3 crore in Q3, driven by a record 2.5 million tonne crushing season. Management said the bio-based chemicals outlook is stronger from Q1 FY27, helped by higher import costs and narrowing fossil-to-bio price gaps, while the 200 KLPD grain distillery is nearing commissioning trials.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability fall from INR95 crore (31 March 2025) to INR66 crore (31 March 2026), and what will profitability look like next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin pressure to a higher sugarcane price for the last season without a matching increase in sugar MSP or ethanol prices. It pointed to better bio-based chemicals and maize ethanol contributions in the coming year, without a figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net realisation on ethanol by feedstock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net realisation is about INR60-plus per litre from B-heavy molasses, INR65-plus from juice and about INR72 from maize; all prices are government-declared.

qa_highlights.question: Has the grain distillery equipment arrived and what margins are underwritten for maize ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all equipment is on site with one or two items pending, and commissioning trials are targeted for next month. Larger benefits are expected from the November ethanol year; management did not give a spread figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the specialty mix fall, and was the ethyl acetate ramp deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was partly a margin call, since ethanol supply is in surplus and ethyl acetate margins were attractive, while the long-term aim is still more specialty chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DME pilot status and what milestones are needed before commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The lab work at ICT is complete and the pilot plant is running; management expects 3 to 6 more months of research before it can give a better answer.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in the ethanol price or policy outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Price revisions are for the government to decide. The industry has asked for higher blend pricing given sugarcane price rises over three years, and management pointed to E85/E100 draft standards as future demand support.

544280|2026-03.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.
544280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18% YoY to INR 2,777 crore and EBITDA dropped to INR 170 crore from INR 415 crore, with a net loss of INR 89 crore. Management blamed customer payment delays, overseas supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict, one-off provisions and marine cost overruns, and failure to cross margin-recognition thresholds on some projects. FY26 revenue was INR 12,322 crore (down 5.4%), EBITDA INR 1,439 crore (11.7% margin) and PAT INR 251 crore after a INR 76 crore Labour Code charge. Management guided FY26 order booking of INR 30,000 crore for FY27 but declined to give revenue or margin guidance until visibility improves.

capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 1,069 crore, of which about INR 700 crore was in Q4; FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore.

FY26 depreciation included INR 454 crore accelerated depreciation on TBMs; normal depreciation about INR 289 crore; Q4 depreciation about INR 100 crore per quarter, expected to rise modestly in FY27 as TBM additions of about INR 1,000 crore hit gross block.
Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 tunnel boring machine second consignment received; tunnelling expected to start before end of next quarter, and the package may extend by 12-15 months.
HRRL crude oil terminal at Mundra commissioned in FY26; Bangalore double-decker metro and Delhi-Meerut RRTS sections operational.

Two Croatia road tenders where Afcons was L1 were cancelled by the client on budget grounds; Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Gondiya L1 positions were removed after rebid instructions, with Pune Ring Road possibly re-tendered around June.
Bid pipeline about INR 4 lakh crore over two years (70% domestic, 30% overseas); FY27 INR 30,000 crore mix stated as about 60% domestic and 40% international.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 customer payments did not come as in the past 15-20 years; Afcons chose liquidity over growth, funding projects only up to limits, and overseas supply disruption in March (fuel, gas, logistics) hit execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Total one-offs of about INR 260-265 crore: about INR 160 crore of Q4 provisions (including an ECL matrix shift), a significant arbitration-related provision, and extra cost on a marine project. Management said no further provisions were made in Q1 FY27 to date.

544280|2026-06.headline: Afcons Q1 FY27 revenue fell 20% to INR2,727 crore and PAT to INR30 crore; management expects H2-weighted recovery with no formal guidance.

Order inflow was strong at INR13,219 crore, lifting order book to INR43,290 crore, while working capital and debt rose. 544282|2026-06.headline: Sagility Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.6% YoY to INR 19,635m; FY27 margin guidance held at 24-25% despite a 120 bps minimum-wage hit.
544282|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 27.6% YoY (15.2% in constant currency) to INR 19,635 million, with organic growth of 27.3% in INR and 14.9% in constant currency, helped by the CareSeed acquisition closed 11 June 2026. Sequentially, reported revenue fell because about $24.8 million of Q4 open-enrolment revenue did not recur, but steady-state organic revenue grew 5.1% QoQ in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.9% to INR 4,716 million at a 24.0% margin (down from 24.9% in Q4), and adjusted PAT rose 35.1% to INR 2,697 million at 13.7%. Management reiterated low double-digit FY27 organic constant-currency growth and the 24-25% margin range, with the wage impact absorbed via efficiencies and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What share of minimum-wage staff is in Karnataka and Telangana, and is the 120 bps impact recurring and recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 15-20% of employees are outside Karnataka and Telangana; the 120 bps impact includes cascading pay-parity effects; full mitigation expected in 12-18 months via efficiencies and expansion in other states.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the low double-digit guidance not higher given 5% QoQ underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ growth should not be extrapolated; 14.9% organic growth in Q1 and confidence in double-digit growth for FY27 were reiterated, with narrower guidance at end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pricing lever in the 15% growth, and what is the split between new and old clients?
qa_highlights.answer: No pricing increases were taken; the client-level split of growth was not available and will be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin guidance not raised despite 24% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-quarter minimum wage impact starts Q2 (about double the Q1 impact); FX gains and efficiencies offset; lower end is expected to be exceeded if the wage impact is lower.

qa_highlights.question: How much seasonal revenue was in FY25 vs FY26 and what drives FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal revenue was about $20 million in Q3+Q4 FY25 (about 3%) and about $50 million in FY26 (about 6%), boosted by BroadPath and a clinical seasonal client; FY27 expected at a similar percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A pipeline focused where?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinical, provider-side and healthcare technology capabilities; direct client-acquisition M&A is difficult given existing vendor relationships.

Currency: management said FX gains (over 100 bps in Q1) helped hold margins; reversal would pressure the 24-25% range.

544282|2026-09.headline: Sagility Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% YoY in INR to INR 20,321 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin hit 26.3%, and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 25-26%.
544282|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 20,321 mn ($212.6 mn), up 22.5% YoY in INR and 12.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 11.9% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to INR 5,353 mn at a 26.3% margin, the highest in six quarters, helped by operating efficiencies, FX tailwinds and geo mix despite higher statutory wage costs. Management acquired Chirok Health LLC (closed October 21, 2026) to build a mid-cycle RCM capability and push provider growth, and raised FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 25-26% from 24-25%. The company now holds a net cash position of INR 1,127 mn, and management expects open enrolment/AEP revenue to be slightly lower than last year.

+23% YoY; margin up from 24% in Q1

segments.commentary: Accounted for 10.1% of Q2 revenue and has grown at about 10-11%, lagging payers. Revenue tapered from some discrete projects with one provider client; Chirok acquisition is intended to accelerate this segment.

segments.commentary: Clinical documentation improvement, medical coding, risk adjustment, HEDIS/quality. TTM revenue to Sep 2026 of $13 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin 35.8%, net revenue retention above 115%, 750+ employees mostly in India. Consideration $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out tied to CY27-CY28 revenue targets.

segments.commentary: Integrated into clinical practice; strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capability and adds mid- and small-sized clients. Contributed to the gap between reported 22.5% and organic 22.2% growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double digits in constant currency maintained; Chirok and CareSeed revenue sits on top of organic guidance.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25%; management said it sees 24-26% as the structural range, with possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained.

OE/AEP revenue expected to be slightly lower than last year, roughly 100 bps lower as a share of total revenue (last year about 6%); marginally below flat YoY per CFO; subject to change over coming weeks.
Management intends to repay all outstanding debt in full during FY27.
Interim dividend of INR 0.15 per share approved, payable in Q3 FY27.
No explicit provider revenue-share target given; management declined to give Chirok guidance until late FY27.
capex_capacity: H1 fixed asset additions INR 1,168 mn; H1 acquisition cash outflow INR 1,338 mn.
Employee strength 51,486 at end Q2; quarterly voluntary attrition 25.7%, down from 28.6% in Q1 FY27 and lower than Q2 FY26.
Delivery centre count fell to 28 from 31 in March 2026 (33 in FY25), but management said this reflects counting multiple facilities on one campus as one site; seat count continued to rise.
Some short-term leases used during site consolidation; Jamaica sites closed earlier.
Staffing to capacity for AEP season with some flex capacity available.
105 active client groups; all top 10 client groups above $20 mn TTM revenue for the first time.
demand_pricing: Deal ACV up 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2, from wins across 31 existing clients and one new client.
Payment integrity win from a Big Ten health plan is contingency-based, so revenue builds over time.
Clients making more deliberate, senior-level buying decisions for large transformation deals; pipeline skewed to managed services and mid-market Blues plans.
Agentic AI deployments: Synchrony Claims Lifecycle (claims adjudication) and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle (denials and appeals), with humans in the loop.
Management said provider deals have historically been smaller; gross margin difference between payer and provider is about 200-300 bps and deal-specific.
On AI pricing, most productivity gains will be passed to clients, with some retained.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what supports the raised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited operating efficiencies, a small FX tailwind from Q1 to Q2, and favourable geo mix; he expects FX to stay broadly at current levels and efficiencies to continue for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much could open enrolment contribution fall this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chirok a step-up in provider mix, and is there an explicit provider target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is there conflict in serving both payers and providers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin stay in 24-26% range or structurally rise with AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the minimum wage impacts and delivery centre trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the full minimum wage impact is baked into guidance (Q2 about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1), with Karnataka and Telangana effective end May and 1 June. The drop in site count reflects campus consolidation.

risks_watch: OE/AEP revenue is running slightly below last year, and the number could still shift over the coming weeks.
Chirok revenue per headcount is well below a listed Indian provider peer; management could not explain the gap and will follow up. Chirok pricing is said to be at market.
Chirok's AI disruption exposure in mid-cycle RCM: management says outpatient coding is most vulnerable, while inpatient coding is less exposed.
Provider growth has lagged payers; watch whether Chirok and cross-selling lift provider growth above 10-11%.
Statutory minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana are a continuing cost headwind; any stay would be upside.
Q2 margin benefited from FX and geo mix, so sustainability depends on FX staying near current levels.
Earn-out payments on Chirok (up to $12.35 mn) and the $10 mn+ payment integrity deal depend on revenue milestones, so timing is uncertain.
Possible acquisitions: management said it stays open to clinical capability or client-focused tuck-ins, but named no specific target.

544283|2026-03.headline: ACME Solar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR705 crore, FY26 revenue INR2,507 crore (+59%), with 2.3 GW of merchant BESS now running.
544283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR705 crore (+31% YoY), including INR157 crore of other income, and FY26 revenue was INR2,507 crore (+59%) on capacity addition and higher CUF. PAT was INR138 crore for the quarter (19.6% margin) and INR498 crore for FY26 (19.9%), with management citing EBITDA margins above 90%. Management said about 2.3 GW of BESS is now commissioned and earning on merchant and short-term contracts at roughly INR2.2 crore per day. Management also flagged a timeline shift: most of the 1.5 GW generation commissioning and the 10 GWh BESS target depend on CTU substations, some of which are delayed by up to about 6 months.

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (operational)
segments.commentary: Operational contracted generation capacity is 2,990 MW. Management said plant and grid availability were above 99% for the year, and FY26 portfolio CUF was about 26%. Sikar (Rajasthan) new plants ran at about 29-30% CUF for the year, and roughly 28%+ in Q4.

segments.name: BESS (merchant)
segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

guidance_outlook: Target of about 1.5 GW of generation projects commissioned in FY27, with the first FDRE commissioning at Neemuch substation in June 2026.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.

Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. 544286|2026-03.headline: Niva Bupa FY26 GWP grew 27.4% to INR9,433 crores and IFRS PAT rose to INR366 crores; FY29 combined ratio target ~99%.

Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.

544286|2026-06.headline: Niva Bupa Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR137.8 crore and CISR improved 300bp to 100.2%, driven by a 3.8pp lower loss ratio.
544286|2026-06.overview: Niva Bupa reported Q1 FY27 profit after tax of INR137.8 crore and a combined insurance service ratio (CISR) of 100.2%, against 103.2% a year earlier. Growth was strong in retail health (reported 47.1%, like-to-like 35.5%) while group business was flat amid a challenging B2B pricing environment. The company moved fully to Ind AS in Q1, with parallel IFRS 17-style disclosures continuing for public reporting. Management said July loss ratio trends were in line with plan and reiterated the FY29 mid-to-high-teens ROE target.

Adjusted EBITDA rose from ₹47 crore to ₹55 crore, and reported PAT of ₹42 crore fell sequentially from ₹66 crore because of a deferred tax item recognised in Q4 FY26. Growth businesses (Super Loads and vehicle finance) grew ~44% QoQ after ~20% QoQ last quarter.

segments.name: Super Loads and vehicle finance (growth businesses)

Fuel business is still uncertain. Management gave no timeline for full recovery in fuel loyalty margins.

Vehicle finance expected to converge to profitability by end of FY27 (reaffirmed).

Super Loads segment-level disclosure expected in about three to four quarters, once the business is large enough.

Telematics device depreciation is front-loaded over two years, which raised depreciation this quarter.
About 40-50% of Super Loads loads are AI-enabled on a given day.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra (Axis Capital): Which hubs is Super Loads present in, daily load volumes, and outlook for the next 1-2 years?

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse (JM Financial): Will the macro headwinds in tolling and fuelling taper in Q2 and FY27?

qa_highlights.answer: Management sees it as a positive for the industry since there is little qualified competition. It sees no near-term threat and will watch market share closely.

qa_highlights.answer: User growth is driven by tolling, telematics and marketplace acquisition, which have been secular for 10-12 quarters. Super Loads is a low-frequency use case and too early to move usage minutes (under 5% of hubs covered).

qa_highlights.question: Monica Joshi: What learnings from earlier cities are being applied to new ones, and how are Bangalore like-for-like numbers trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New cities are layered and run with several parallel experiments; AI-first, less people-dependent workflows are used. Management declined to give like-for-like Bangalore numbers until the segment is large enough to report separately.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: For the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax. The loss-utilisation position will be reassessed at the end of the year (Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

H2 FY26 revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹990 Cr, but H2 EBITDA margin (11.4%) and PAT margin (8.5%) were lower than full-year levels, which management attributed to billing mix. Order inflow for FY26 was ₹2,743 Cr and the unexecuted order book closed at ₹3,326 Cr, below the ~₹4,500 Cr previously flagged, which management blamed on delayed tender results. Receivables rose sharply to ~₹350 Cr, which management attributed to heavy March billing, and payables rose to about 58 days.

Insurance surety bonds now used in ~8-10% of non-Gujarat orders and expected to rise as more states include the clause in tenders.

544292|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% QoQ to INR4,282 million and EBITDA reached INR919 million, while management reiterated the FY28 target of US$400 million revenue at ~40% EBITDA margin.

544293|2026-06.headline: Suraksha Diagnostic Q1 FY27 total income rose 21% YoY to INR 887 million, with PAT up 40% to INR 128 million and EBITDA margin at 36%.

544294|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 62% YoY to about INR142 crores; FY26 revenue up 87% to INR485 crores, but margins fell and management guided to similar growth in FY27.

For FY26, revenue rose 87% to INR485 crores, PBT rose from INR10 crores to INR28 crores, and EBITDA rose from INR38 crores to INR66 crores. Margins were lower than previously guided, which management attributed to qualification and investment costs for new semiconductor and space customers. Management guided to similar growth in FY27 and said margins would improve, and it is pursuing a QIP sized at about 7-10% of market cap.

544296|2026-03.headline: Nisus standalone core revenue rose 110% YoY to INR 141 crore and PAT to INR 68 crore (48% margin) in FY26, with Q4 PAT of INR 11 crore.
544296|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year as a listed company, and management said core standalone revenue (ex-NCCCL) of INR 141 crore beat the INR 120-140 crore guidance despite a Q4 slowdown tied to West Asia conflict. Q4 core PAT was INR 11 crore, and the consolidated group (including NCCCL, acquired August 2025) reported revenue of INR 575 crore and PAT of INR 83 crore. Management said UAE transactions worth over INR 500 crore were deferred rather than lost, and FY27 guidance is presented as a two-scenario framework rather than a point estimate. NCCCL's PAT rose to INR 16.4 crore from INR 3.5 crore, and its order book was INR 1,833 crore at March-end, plus INR 870 crore added in April-May 2026.

financial_highlights.change: ~4.7x from INR 3.5 crore; NCCCL top line up ~7%

segments.name: Fund and asset management (core)
segments.commentary: Management said fund and asset management is now about 55% of core revenue versus advisory at about 45%; fee income is largely from sponsor capital in own funds plus treasury/investment income. UAE GCC portfolio of four assets reported 30% NAV growth in latest valuation, with management saying no impairment.

segments.name: Transaction advisory (core)
segments.commentary: Advisory held firm in Q4 despite the UAE transaction slowdown and was described as the counter-cyclical offset; advisory share was 67% of revenue when the business started versus about 55% now.

segments.commentary: Order book INR 1,833 crore at 31 March 2026, plus INR 870 crore added in first two months of FY27 (management cites ~INR 2,600-2,700 crore total). Repaid about 65% of acquisition debt (INR 38 crore outstanding at March 31); EBITDA margin about 9%, PAT margin about 2-3%.

segments.commentary: Presented as a separate digital asset business in the UAE entity; awaiting token issuance licence and white paper approval, with live launch hoped for within FY27. No financial contribution quantified.

FY27 revenue-to-AUM ratio assumed at around 2.85% (blended), with management calling 3% a steady-state assumption versus 5.3-5.6% in FY26, which included one-off UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains.
NCCCL FY27 target of about INR 850 crore revenue; management aims for 3-4x turnover over the next year per Vice Chairman, with EBITDA margins of 9-10%.
REIC Ops fund (launched 2019) expected to wind up in 2026, with management fee booking expected more likely in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline: India about INR 700 crore (60-70% at term sheet); UAE about INR 2,000 crore being renegotiated on entry prices; management expects India deployment over the next couple of quarters.

Two India transactions (about INR 150 crore each) slipped by a few months due to Pune land demarcation methodology change, lender committee NOC delays, and RERA/e-Khata issues in Gujarat, Karnataka and Telangana; management expects these to close in the current quarter.
UAE deferred deals: one INR 500 crore transaction and one INR 300 crore transaction pushed to later closure.
NCCCL migrating to SAP HANA and adopting digital project management tools.
demand_pricing: Dubai: off-plan share fell from about 78% last year to much smaller levels as ready-to-move-in inventory rose to about 60-70%; investor purchases fell from about 87% (2017-18) to about 45%, with end-users at about 55%.

Dubai pricing: management cited 10-15% discounts from January levels in Dubai and 5% in Abu Dhabi, with a weighted average market discount of roughly 15-20%; management said its own assets were up around 30% in valuation.
Management said it is buying at discounts to market and that renegotiation of entry prices is underway on the INR 2,000 crore UAE pipeline.
NCCCL works on 3-4 year order book visibility; industry EBITDA norm 9-10%, PAT 3-4%.
Management said advisory fees are directly correlated with AUM and fund size, and that the blended AUM-fee mix should shift toward management fees over time.

qa_highlights.question: What regulatory or lender-approval delays pushed India transactions out, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said Pune demarcation methodology changed, and consortium lender NOCs took longer (March to May); about two trades of roughly INR 150 crore each slipped by a few months and are expected this quarter. Gujarat RERA and Bengaluru e-Khata were also cited as slowing approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neon Fund size, fees and timing, and REIC Ops closure economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Aanchal Singh said SEBI approval for the Neon Fund came the previous day, with launch from Q2; INR 1,800 crore fund plus INR 500 crore green shoe, fees broadly INR 220 crore, 7.5-year tenure. REIC Ops has a 12% hurdle with no catch-up, closing this year, with fees more likely in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core run-rate fee income excluding one-time investment gains, and how does revenue compare to cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the segment reporting does not split recurring fees from treasury income; fee income is described as small relative to the fund and asset management segment, which includes treasury income from sponsor capital in own funds. No quantified run-rate was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue-to-AUM assumed at 2.85% versus 5.3% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was inflated by high-margin UAE advisory contracts and book investment gains on yield compression; 3% is the steady-state assumption, and capital is expected to deploy mainly in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the India (INR 700 crore) and UAE (INR 2,000 crore) pipelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Avadhoot Sarwate said 60-70% of the India pipeline is at term sheet stage, with deployment in the next couple of quarters. For UAE, management said 50-60% of the pipeline is at a complete stage, and at least INR 800 crore of transactions were deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee costs rise to 32% of revenue, and what is the outlook for NCCCL margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new hires, annual appraisals, and a change to accrual-based bonus accounting from this year. NCCCL margins target 9-10% EBITDA with 2-3% PAT, with growth coming from volume.

risks_watch: UAE real estate weakness: off-plan decline, lower investor demand, and deferrals of INR 500-800 crore deals; management did not give a timeline for stabilisation.

Tokenisation and Neon fund launches depend on regulatory approvals (token licence and white paper; SEBI approved Neon fund).

544305|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA positive at INR 174 mn (5.9% margin) and PAT INR 44 mn; FY26 EBITDA still negative INR 52 mn after heavy reinvestment.
544305|2026-03.overview: MobiKwik reported back-to-back EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarters in Q3 and Q4 FY26, with Q4 total income of INR 2,960 mn (+6% YoY) and contribution margin of 46% versus 23% a year earlier. FY26 EBITDA improved to negative INR 52 mn from negative INR 794 mn, and full-year PAT narrowed to negative INR 621 mn from negative INR 1,215 mn. Management said it is deliberately reinvesting core payments and lending profits (about INR 55 crore spent in FY26) into four growth engines: offline and online merchant payments, an NBFC, and AI. Analysts pressed on the gap between UPI-led GMV growth and flat payments revenue, on the timing of breakeven for merchant businesses, and on NBFC rollout.

qa_highlights.answer: INR 55 crore was invested in FY26, and a similar range is expected in FY27. Everything except device capitalisation hits P&L, and IPO proceeds are being used for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the merchant breakeven timeline move from 3-4 quarters to FY28, and what does baseline profitability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs were raised deliberately to build new businesses; without the merchant investment FY26 EBITDA would have been about INR 50 crore. Management aims to stay PAT-positive while reinvesting, with FY27 EBITDA hypothetically between 1x and 2x of the reinvested base.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited gross take rate moderation and mix shift to lower-margin categories; the non-UPI revenue growth has been below expectations.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

risks_watch: Payments revenue dip from paused card-linked categories (credit and debit, rent, education); relaunch targeted for Q2 FY27 and not yet proven.
Lending disbursements fell in Q1; Q2 INR1,000 crore run rate depends on the digital lending transfer closing in August 2026 without disruption.
Gross take-rate compression as UPI (near-zero take rate) and merchant volumes grow; net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps long term versus 13-15 bps recently.
Net financial services margin of 5.9% in Q1 includes write-backs (about 18% of gross lending revenue); management guides 4.5-5.5% long term.
Merchant business still loss-making (FY27 burn INR50-60 crore); merchant revenue, device and merchant counts not disclosed; breakeven FY28.
Regulatory dependence: PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI; no timeline given.
Own NBFC launch still 'some time away'; CoR pending until digital lending transfer completes.
Q1 PAT of INR76 million rests on one quarter; full-year PAT of about INR400 million requires sustained sequential improvement of about INR20-30 million per quarter.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.
544305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and guidance, with a repeated 'fairly confident' stance on FY27 PAT and EBITDA targets. Cautious and evasive on merchant metrics (no merchant counts, devices or revenue, calling it 'too early'), on regulatory issues around UPI MDR (expressed frustration), and on the timing of its own NBFC.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Platform GMV up 50% YoY to INR587bn, merchant GMV up 17% QoQ, and lending disbursements guided from ~INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter with Q2 already at that rate; payments volume is strong but card-linked categories are paused and relaunch is not yet proven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the ~INR25 crore of residual IPO-funded merchant devices; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.why: Management targets INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter from cross-sell, with 60% of Q1 loans going to repeat customers, but no conversion data has been disclosed yet.

rows.label: PPI-on-UPI MDR rollout by NPCI
rows.why: RBI mandated the PPI-on-UPI MDR but NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years and gave no timeline, so there is no visible monetisation in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 PAT of ~INR400m and EBITDA of ~INR750m and the INR1,000 crore lending run rate, but cautious and evasive on merchant counts, devices and revenue, UPI MDR, and NBFC timing; analysts pushed on the sustainability of the Q1 profit and the falling lending disbursements.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.
544306|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FTE model, with a long-term framing; cautious and evasive on quarterly guidance, customer-level revenue, and capex phasing beyond FY27. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.
Generally, we don't quantify what we're doing with each customer.

rows.why: Management expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27; one FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2 with work from Q3, and ~65% of customers now use integrated discovery services.

rows.when: end-Q2 FY27 close, work from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Another large pharma process development FTE deal is expected to close by end-Q2, and three of four commercial contracts were added in Q1 (three commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotal).
