rows.when: FY27, one more in Q2 FY28
rows.why: One Phase 3 customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, and one expected Q2 FY28, supporting future CDMO commercial volumes.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FTE model, Discovery sold out and H2 capacity ramp, but cautious on quarterly CDMO lumpiness, customer-level revenue and capex phasing beyond FY27; analysts pushed on why 15-20% guidance holds given slowing recent quarters and the 6% CDMO growth.

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
544307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management said it is difficult to model the West Asia situation and fuel price impact.
Private-brand discount to market leaders on apparel (about 40%) to remain at least the same, with a possible wider gap.
Store expansion will not slow; management said it aims to open more stores where practical.
Input inflation (petroleum-linked plastics, polyester, detergent inputs) is starting to flow through; full impact expected in the balance of May and June.
Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.
Working capital cycle expected to stay at FY26 levels, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: Store count 795 at March 2026 after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4); presence in 535 cities after adding 77 cities in FY26.
47 of the 105 FY26 openings were in South India (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka); 5 in Gujarat and 3 in Maharashtra.
Trading area 1.34 crore sq ft at March 2026.
Karnataka store areas reduced in many stores; sales per sq ft has risen and is now in line with the national average, per CFO.
Lease escalation about 15% every three years (about 5% a year), per CFO.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 SSSG acceleration to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST rate cuts, plus extra investment in growth and promotions.
FY26 SSSG of 11% split: 7 points from new customers and transactions, 2 points from more items per customer, 2 points from higher price points.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred to the Board and gave no dividend commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kerala is above average, Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) are in line with the network, and small-format stores match large-format stores on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cleared old spring/summer stock ahead of the April-June season and increased promotions to capture a consumption uptick. The CFO said working capital days are about the same as last year and that is the intended operating level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (petroleum derivatives, plastics, polyester, fabric at 10-11%) reaching shelf prices from May-June, and its effect on SSSG and gross margin.
Q4 gross margin compression linked to promotions; whether promotional intensity stays high into the April-June season.
Geopolitical and crude-price shocks, currency depreciation and possible weak rural demand from a poor monsoon.
Vendor labour and gas availability constraints, which the company says are easing.
Rising competition in apparel from e-commerce and value-fashion players moving into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.
544307|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on private-brand resilience, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to model the West Asia and fuel-price impact and said the coming months could be challenging. It was evasive on dividend policy, deferring to the Board.
key_quotes: So, it is clearly correlated with crude pricing in that sense.
We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country.
So, our pricing is totally consumer -led.

544307|2026-06.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
544307|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 819 stores in 559 cities at June 2026 end after 27 openings in the quarter, including 10 in South India; total trading area 13.8 million sq ft.

segments.name: Small format
segments.commentary: 3 small stores opened in the quarter (16 in total cited); currently run only in UP and Haryana, with a stated opportunity of about 3,000 small-format stores nationally.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: Contributed 75.2% of revenue; 100% of apparel, about 75% of general merchandise, about 60% by volume of FMCG, and about 50% of kitchen appliances (Tandem brand).

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: 767 stores across 520 cities and over 1.4 crore registered consumers; contributes 2-9% of store revenue, at least 5% in most locations; average bill about INR 800; 20% of customers are new to Vishal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper in subsequent quarters.
Small-format stores to accelerate; current guidance cited as 80 to 100 small-format store additions.
RFID rollout: Delhi NCR stores live; full network rollout expected to slightly exceed one year.
No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.
Gross margin sustainability depends on current cost structure; management says no significant issue if circumstances hold, but declined to forecast West Asia-linked developments.
Foreign ownership to be capped at 49.99% to keep the company Indian owned and controlled; foreign holding is close to 20% today.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 27 in Q1 FY27 (819 total); small-format openings were slow at 3 in the quarter, with some large-format stores opened alongside.
New format: first pilot store said to be very close to launch, followed by one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision.
RFID: pilot in 2 stores in Delhi NCR, now extended to all Delhi NCR stores; stock counts possible in 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts.
Minimum wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others lifted employee cost per sq ft about 13% YoY.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Price increases were limited to higher price points and selected categories; opening and mid price points were not raised, and price-sensitive categories such as children's clothing and staple foods were left unchanged.
Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?

544309|2026-03.headline: IKS agreed to acquire TruBridge for ~$557M enterprise value (~3x EBITDA), funded by $565M debt; management guides to ~INR3,000 crore revenue ambition by FY30.
544309|2026-03.overview: IKS signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire TruBridge, a US listed EHR and RCM provider, on April 23, 2026, with closing expected in 90 to 120 days subject to HSR/FTC clearance. TruBridge's trailing CY2025 revenue was $347M ($126M EHR, $221M RCM) and adjusted EBITDA was $69M, versus $186M-plus on a reported-to-adjusted basis cited by management. Management framed the deal as adding an EHR installed base of about 700 clients as a distribution and data moat for IKS's AI-led RCM and clinical workflow platform. The call focused on strategic rationale and TAM, with limited detail on synergy quantum or timing beyond G&A-first sequencing and a four-year timeline.

Management will not change its aspirations to grow faster than the ~12% US industry rate; it expects to be fairly confident on margin but less certain on growth over 2-3 years.

Small language models (SLMs) sitting on top of LLMs are planned to reduce compute and build proprietary self-learning loops for RCM.
Acute RCM offering to be launched; Scribble ambient scribing product to be upgraded into a live encounter co-pilot.
Management described the EHR modernisation as costly for TruBridge, previously a drain on financials, and said IKS would bring agile, cost-optimised development.
demand_pricing: RCM is fragmented: top players hold under 20% share, with 400-plus players and a long tail; US healthcare RCM spend about $1.75-1.8 trillion, of which management's modelled addressable base is around 2% take rate.
Management modelled 2% take rate for RCM outsourcing (versus about 3% today) to conservatively allow for price compression from AI.

Competitors named: Med-Metrix and CorroHealth (RCM BPO); 3M and Optum (encoders); Epic, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen (EHR); Oracle Cerner challenger; MEDITECH; Phreesia, Augmedix, Abridge, Ambience and Microsoft DAX in ambient AI.
Management argues outcome-based pricing will replace per-user SaaS pricing as AI orchestrates tasks; TruBridge's 700-client base is outpatient-heavy (60-70% of volume).
Management said the parent's own attempts at globalising RCM and building a captive in India had not succeeded, and that IKS brings an offshore-enabled model.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR is a two-player market with Epic and Oracle Cerner dominant and MEDITECH a challenger; RCM is largely unmanaged, and about 230-240 of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients already buy RCM, leaving a large white space. The 500-odd clients without RCM and 1,500 non-TruBridge EHR clients are targets.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the initial synergies or the financial outcome of the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify synergies beyond saying the INR1,000 crore to INR3,000 crore north star is a definition of success, and said the target contains uncertainty for learnings and mistakes; drivers are RCM transformation, globalisation and G&A, with 2,000-plus RCM FTEs in India versus about 1,000 in US.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deal structured with a 4-year timeline and why is the organic path hard?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergy timing is not being given in detail; G&A synergies come first and operational synergies later; organic growth to 700 clients would take about a decade and IKS's global RCM model is a differentiator given earlier failed attempts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steps post-close and how will IKS retain customers and talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management outlined Q1 learning, Q2 actioning new structure, Q3 operational synergies; customer retention was called the gold mine of the transaction, along with identifying and retaining key talent in the first quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How does TruBridge's headcount and RCM proposition compare with IKS's model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR has low marginal cost and RCM is tech-led and AI-first; RCM spend at large systems runs about 4-5% of revenue and about 7-10% at hospitals, strengthening the outsourcing proposition.

qa_highlights.question: Does IKS plan to compete with the large EHR vendors at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is not to take EHR to larger hospitals; EHR is for the 0-50 bed segment, with the 50-200 bed range a later addition, and EHR is to be a sticky source of data for RCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth guidance change after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not changing aspirations of growing faster than the ~12% industry rate, and is less certain on growth than margins over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intangible amortisation schedule is being separately evaluated for EHR and RCM relationships, with new asset lives under valuation by experts; the $5M accretion was presented as the highest-possible level, with minor changes possible.

qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?

544318|2026-03.headline: Mamata Machinery FY26 revenue fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 8.2%, which management attributes mainly to a 50% US decline and one-offs.
544318|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a consolidation year: revenue from operations fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore (FY25: Rs 254.6 crore) and Q4 revenue was Rs 73.9 crore versus Rs 111 crore a year earlier. The US business (including Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, hit by unresolved tariffs through Q2-Q3, then West Asia uncertainty and higher polymer prices in Q4. EBITDA fell to Rs 19.1 crore (8.2% margin) from Rs 54.6 crore (21.4%), and PAT to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 40.8 crore. Management says the company remains debt-free with Rs 69.26 crore cash and guides FY27 revenue growth of about 15% with margin normalisation toward about 20%.

segments.commentary: Packaging revenue was flat to down about 1%, at roughly Rs 48-49 crore. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore, while domestic packaging grew about 55%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the FSA exemption and three-year carry-forward mean packaging users face minimal near-term compliance pressure, making FY27-28 the inflection point?

qa_highlights.question: Are there other markets to diversify into if the US stays weak? What is the Russia revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging is being taken to Africa and Europe in FY27; a Russia branch office was approved. Russia has no packaging revenue yet, only a couple of converting machines. Converting is already present in about 84 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split and margin difference between exports and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 89.59 crore: 62% exports, 38% domestic. Gross margin about 60% on exports vs about 42-43% domestically. Rs 80 crore executes in H1 FY27 and Rs 9 crore in H2 FY27.

544319|2026-03.headline: Senores FY26 consolidated revenue rose 62% to about INR664 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR122 crore; FY27 guided to 30-40% revenue growth.
544319|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 66% YoY to about INR190 crore, with EBITDA of INR62 crore (32.7% margin, up about 1,151 bps) and PAT after minority interest of about INR32 crore (up 78%). Regulated markets drove the quarter at INR118 crore (up 83%), while emerging markets grew 26% and India branded generics roughly doubled to about INR9 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and PAT growth of 50-60%, with blended EBITDA margin held at 29-31%. The Apnar Pharma acquisition (75% stake, 25% due by year-end) weighed on working capital and margin in Q4, with commercial shipments only starting in April 2026.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US and others)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR427 crore, up 75%; Q4 INR118 crore, up 83%, driven by portfolio expansion. Sourced/spot business is 10-12% of total revenue and is not expected to grow.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR145 crore, up 20%. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter with EBITDA margin of 18-19%; management expects this margin to hold, and the segment is now cash-flow positive. FY27 revenue projection is about INR180 crore.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR40 crore, roughly 5x FY25. FY26 budget is INR60-70 crore; about 120-130 MRs in field, with a long-run plateau of about 200 MRs.

segments.name: CDMO-CMO and own products
segments.commentary: Management says own products are about 50-53% and CDMO-CMO about 47-48% of revenue. Apnar facility is expected to contribute INR80-100 crore in FY27 and INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 30-40%, with PAT growth of about 50-60%; management called 30-35% the minimum achievable and will review after one or two quarters.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at 29-31% for FY27; ex-other-income, Q4 FY26 margin of 26.5% could be about 28-28.5%.
Apnar Pharma FY27 revenue budgeted at INR80-100 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue expected at INR10-20 crore; INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.

Capex FY27 about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables and the balance for other plants and maintenance; management expects FCF generation in FY27.
Long-term aspiration of INR2,500-3,000 crore (up to INR4,000 crore) US revenue in 3-4 years across India and US facilities; ANDA rollout of 90-95% of the 51 approved ANDAs within 6-8 quarters.

FY27 capex expected at about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables; about INR100 crore IPO proceeds earmarked for sterile manufacturing, to be started within this year.

Emerging markets PIC/S approval for the facility expected around June-July 2026; more than 4,000 products under registration in emerging markets.
demand_pricing: Approved ANDAs rose from 22 (March 2025) to 51 (March 2026), covering more than 150 strengths; 20-21 launched, 30 to be launched over next few quarters; about 27 further molecules (60+ strengths) in development.
Management estimates the total accessible market for currently approved products plus pipeline at close to $1 billion.
Emerging market realisation per unit rose from about INR1.20 to about INR1.90 over 1-1.5 years (about 60-70%), with a shift to niche molecules.
Amerisyn JV (entered April 2026) targets US federal, VA and military procurement and FSS tenders; management says margins are not thin.
Management says branded generics do not need a large MR expansion to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net working capital days rise from 114 to 187, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the jump is due to Apnar being consolidated with no sales yet; excluding Apnar, the cycle is about 104 days. Apnar is expected to align with group cycle from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is other financial assets of INR172 crore (previously unbilled revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is profit share on cost-plus B2B supplies, booked as income and parked as a financial asset until realised, typically 1-6 months. Balance should plateau then fall as launches mature. Not warranty or royalty.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance conservative given 60% growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited external uncertainty (shipping, US inflation) and said 30-35% is the minimum achievable; guidance to be revisited after one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging market margin improvement: forex versus operations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin gain mainly came from product mix; forex contributed about INR3 crore of realised gains in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate jump from about 17% in FY25 to about 23.6% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to the Apnar tax provision, US tax at 20-21%, and India at 26%, and to FY25 benefit from US carry-forward losses. Long-term rate guided at about 23%.

544319|2026-06.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.
544319|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR180 crores, up 36% YoY, led by regulated markets (up 42%) and emerging markets (up 30%). EBITDA was INR54 crores (up 87%, margin ~30%, up 810 bps) and PAT was INR31 crores (up 56%). Sequentially, absolute EBITDA and PAT dipped versus Q4 FY26, which management attributed mainly to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that did not recur. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and a INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue ambition in three to four years, while the company shifted INR100 crores of IPO proceeds from sterile injectables to oral solids capacity.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY27. ANDA portfolio rose from 30 (June 2025) to about 58 approved (June 2026), with 23 commercialised and 35 planned over the next 18-20 months.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY; EBITDA margin was about 14% (mid-teens) against about 20% in Q4 FY26. Management guides 18-20% for the full year and says the business is cash flow positive, with INR18 crores operating cash in Q1.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR8 crores in Q1 FY27. Management shifted focus to profitability, targeting INR50-60 crores for FY27 at 35-40% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Apnar facility (Baroda, USFDA approved)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 80-90% of production capacity, though much of it goes to qualification and launch batches. About six products have been commercialised from Apnar, and about 30 million units were produced in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-40% and PAT growth of about 50-60%, with similar growth expected thereafter.
Revenue ambition of INR2,500-3,000 crores in three to four years, based on the current pipeline and excluding NDA products; management said variance of 5-10% is possible in any given year.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, with a run rate of INR60-75 crores in the following year.
Emerging market EBITDA margin target of 18-20% on a full-year basis.
Branded generics FY27 revenue target of INR50-60 crores, with 30-40% YoY growth expected.
Zoraya (US front-end) and Amerisyn (US government business) expected to become operational around September-October 2026.
Management expects a 70:30 regulated to emerging market revenue mix to hold for at least the next few years.
Chhatral facility PIC/S approval targeted around Q2-Q3 FY27, opening access to markets such as Vietnam, South Africa and Mexico.
capex_capacity: Apnar (Baroda) facility is at about 80-90% production capacity utilisation, though a large part goes to product qualification and launches. Third production line is under work and a fourth is planned.
Capex is being spent on oral solid capacity in the US and India, plus a scaled-down sterile injectable pilot plant. Shareholder approval for the object change is pending.
Sterile injectable project has about INR100 crores of IPO proceeds left, now pushed to the second half of FY27 with a pilot approach.
Of the 18 products mapped for Apnar, about six are commercialised; portfolio rationalisation between US and India sites is planned from next year.
Management said the Chhatral site in Ahmedabad is PIC/S inspected and makes oral solids, injectables and liquids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did emerging market EBITDA margin fall from about 20% in Q4 FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weaker than H2, and Q1 is still the strongest first quarter in four years. Management reiterated the full-year 18-20% margin target and cited product mix and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded generics decline 2%, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus has moved from sales to profitability after the business rose from INR8 crores to INR40 crores in FY26. It targets INR50-60 crores at 35-40% EBITDA margin for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'other income' restated for June 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no restatement or policy change. Forex gains were moved from above the operating line into other income, so the presentation changed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sequential EBITDA and PAT decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 included about INR14-15 crores of forex gains that were nil in Q1 FY27. Excluding this, margins are in line sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO proceeds use changed from sterile injectables to oral solids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Apnar acquisition and oral solid pipeline growth needed capacity sooner, so it reallocated proceeds to oral solid lines in the US and India. A small sterile injectable pilot will follow, and shareholder approval is pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and what is Apnar's utilisation and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, and the run rate is INR60-75 crores after that. Apnar utilisation is 80-90% but partly used for qualification; revenue was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 PAT growth be similar to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a FY28 number and pointed to the INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue goal in three to four years. It said the EBITDA margin of about 30% is the minimum to sustain.

For FY26, revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore, EBITDA rose 33% to INR2,475 million, and PAT rose 48% to INR1,306 million. 544320|2026-06.headline: Carraro India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% on pass-through lag from commodity and freight inflation.
544320|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, driven by domestic growth of about 26% that offset a roughly 14% fall in exports. EBITDA rose 6% YoY to INR579 million, but margin was 10.4% as higher energy, raw material and freight costs, plus supplier-side labour shortages, were not yet recovered from customers. Total income included a one-time INR88 million provision write-back linked to a customs reassessment, which flatters other income and PAT. Management expects the price pass-through gap to close over about 12 months and targets full recovery of price increments for the full year.

Management said the reported figures include a INR 74 crore FX gain in Q4 (INR 138 crore for FY26), and underlying Q4 EBITDA growth was 8% after adjusting for FX. Growth was rate-led in India, volume and TRevPAR-led in Maldives, and annuity was steady, while March 2026 disruption from Middle East tensions and travel advisories dented the strong run-rate. Net debt fell to INR 1,484 crore (1.14x net debt/EBITDA vs 1.7x), and management said growth capex will be funded mainly from internal accruals.

544321|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
544321|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline of about INR16 crores
Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs
Includes INR102 crore net deferred tax liability reversal from tax regime change; tax rate cut from 34.94% to 25.17%

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR203 crores (+13%) and EBITDA INR74 crores (+16%); occupancy rose about 7% to 67% and ADR about 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 20%. Adjusted for a one-off electricity benefit in the prior year, EBITDA growth would be 18%.

segments.name: Maldives resorts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

segments.name: Hospitality total
segments.commentary: Hospitality EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR106 crores; adjusted hospitality EBITDA growth was about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove simultaneous occupancy and ADR gains in India in a seasonally soft quarter, and is there headroom in Pune?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Pune dominance (about 65% of luxury inventory), MICE, corporate demand in IT/BFSI micro markets and weddings; it expects Pune occupancy to stabilise in the high 70s and sees 200-300 luxury and upper-upscale room nights a day added from office growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where do India margins settle, and is there operating leverage beyond cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the solar capex (about INR60 crores, 3-year payback) could add roughly 4-5% to margin from Q1 next year, and that high occupancy is driving operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is Maldives demand doing in April-June, July and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: India source-market demand rose to about 9% from 6%; China and Russia grew at double-digit occupancy; July tourist arrivals were back to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights versus about 170 earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Sahyadri/Kelzai acquisition be funded, and what is the threshold for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said funding will mix debt and internal accruals, with tourism incentive subsidies of 15-20% of capital expected and operations in about 2 to 2.5 years; debt to be drawn in stages as needed. The acquisition criteria answer was not captured clearly in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Maldives EBITDA decline was diesel versus operations, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline entirely to fuel: fuel bill up INR17 crores plus INR2 crores indirect, total about INR19 crores; ex-fuel Maldives EBITDA would have grown about 10%. Diesel was still about 20% below spot due to cluster procurement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goa Hilton performance and expansion timing and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy and revenue are improving post-acquisition (104 keys), gave no unit-level numbers, and said the 50-plus key extension and refurbishment are in planning, with delivery around FY29-FY30; it expects to conservatively double EBITDA with the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sri Lanka Arugam Bay commissioning moved from FY28 to around FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Permissions are the constraint due to environmental sensitivity, about 1.5 km of shoreline and adjacency to Yala National Park; completions and formalities are near, with target around FY30.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify August EBITDA margin, which depends on the war; it said occupancy remains strong and bookings on the books for Q3 and Q4 look very strong.

544322|2026-03.headline: Unimech to acquire Hobel Bellows for about INR450 crore EV, all-cash from internal funds, at roughly 7x EV/EBITDA on ~INR129 crore FY26 revenue and >50% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-03.overview: Unimech announced the acquisition of Hobel Bellows, a metallic bellows and precision assemblies maker, via a subsidiary, for about INR450 crore EV on an all-cash basis funded from internal balance sheet cash. Management said Hobel reported about INR129 crore revenue for FY26 with EBITDA margin above 50%, and projected 15-17% growth over 3-4 years on existing customers without new-customer wins. Management said the core business saw demand recovery and better Q4 FY26 momentum, and that the FTWZ facility awaits only customs clearance, expected by end-May 2026. Q&A centred on customer concentration (two OEM groups ~93% of revenue), valuation rationale, NPCIL and AS9100 certification timelines, and capacity utilisation of 50-60%.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - metallic bellows
segments.commentary: Over 75% of Hobel revenue per management; bellows range 2 to 16 inches, 500 g to 330 kg, for engines of 900 to 9,000 BHP. About 70% of products are single-source.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - exhaust manifolds and structural components
segments.commentary: Remainder of revenue (under 25%) per management; margins said to be similar to bellows.

segments.name: Unimech core business
segments.commentary: Management said demand is normalising after a muted prior year, with improved momentum in Q4 FY26 and a healthy order book; no quantified figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management guides 15-17% growth over the next 3-4 years for Hobel, described as conservative and excluding new customers.
Synergies expected mainly on revenue (cross-selling, nuclear, marine/naval, aerospace), not cost; cost optimisation described as limited.
No new borrowings planned; no major capex expected near term beyond maintenance, with capex deferred until utilisation reaches 80-90%.
FTWZ facility: all approvals received, only customs clearance pending, expected by end-May 2026; delayed versus earlier timelines.
NPCIL qualification expected in about one year; AS9100 certification needed before aerospace work, timing not specified.
Payback on the acquisition estimated at 8-10 years (initial calculation).
capex_capacity: Hobel operates from a 200,000 sq ft facility plus 20,000 sq ft warehouse in Visakhapatnam SEZ; current utilisation 50-60%.
Management targets 85-90% utilisation before deploying new capex; automation and robotics expected to lift effective capacity.
Unimech had planned about INR100 crore capex for metal forming, tube bending and sheet metal; acquisition used instead.
Recent machinery additions include FANUC welding robots, seam welders, automated underwater leak test machine and 3D printer; some yet to be commissioned.
Management said no additional capex needed for AS9100 certification.
demand_pricing: Management cites a global metallic bellows addressable market of about $2.6 billion growing ~6% annually.
Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of Hobel revenue; end uses include power generation, locomotive engines, automotive and industrial systems; exports ~90%.
Cummins QSK95 gensets are an end use; Hobel's wallet share with Cummins described as small.
Margins attributed to high entry barriers, long qualification cycles, proprietary drawings and pricing power rather than cost; previous competitors were European and American.
Management says it will not sacrifice margins for growth, including avoiding automotive volume segments.
Aerospace and semiconductor customers have shown initial interest in tube bending and metal forming capabilities; no quantified pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the seller exiting at ~7x EV/EBITDA when peers trade at 25-30x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the promoter had no succession plan (daughters settled abroad) and had crossed retirement age, so wanted an exit to a suitable buyer.

qa_highlights.question: What is client concentration and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of revenue across 10-12 geographies; about INR60 crore working capital retained and monthly cash generation said to be sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CCD a dilution risk and what are its terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCD is an internal instrument between holding and subsidiary, with no near-term intent to convert and negligible interest; the transaction is all cash apart from a 10% holdback for one year.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be amortisation or goodwill?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no amortisation because the investment is in a subsidiary; fixed assets are small and the deal is capability-led and asset-light.

qa_highlights.question: Can Hobel supply NPCIL reactor-island components such as expansion joints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hobel is not NPCIL certified; qualification is needed, taking about a year, and tubular assemblies are the target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between bellows and manifolds, and by industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Bellows over 75%, with manifolds and other structural components the rest; industry-level split not available and to be taken offline.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: two OEM groups ~93% of revenue, with a single-source product base.
Execution risk on FTWZ customs clearance (expected end-May 2026) after prior delays.
Aerospace and nuclear expansion depends on AS9100 and NPCIL qualification, with timelines of roughly one year or more.
Growth guidance (15-17%) is below the analyst view of 10% standalone CAGR being conservative and Cummins-linked demand; watch actual growth.
Retention of senior and technical staff at Hobel, with compensation benchmarking and ESOPs planned over the medium term.
Integration of metal forming and tube bending operations, which stay at the Hobel facility.
544322|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the strategic and margin story, but guarded on growth and certification timelines. Management was non-committal on aggressive growth targets, NPCIL, and the CCD, and deferred several detailed questions (installed capacity, industry split) offline.
key_quotes: This debt-free business acquisition is margin accretive with strong annual cash generation, enhancing the overall quality of Unimech's earnings profile.
So instead of taking, you know, 18 to 24 months to build this organically, we now get immediate access to those opportunities.

The intent for the first 12 months or the short term I should say will always be a slow moving, but eventually when the synergies are going to catch up, so over a medium term you will see the growth coming up.
So it's basically exhaust systems, fuel lines in a high temperature are some of the applications in the aerospace.

544322|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR108 crore, up 71% YoY and 32% QoQ, with Hobel Bellows contributing about INR22 crore over two months. PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.name: Precision component and assembly (PCA)
segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.

Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Order execution timeline, current order pipeline and nuclear order book outlook (INR87 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR280 crore order book is confirmed POs only, excluding FACC forecasts. Tooling backlog mostly gets consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, and nuclear INR87 crore runs into H2 FY27 with some portion in FY28. New nuclear bits are in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and gross/EBITDA margin range for FY27, and capex needs?

qa_highlights.question: Tooling mix between engine and airframe, and growth from SKU expansion versus existing programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise mix but said it is dominated by aero engine components, with airframe tooling an opportunity being explored. Growth will come from both SKU expansion and underlying end-consumer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Where Unimech sits in the value chain across precision components and aerospace?
qa_highlights.answer: In semiconductors and PCA it is already Tier-1 and deals directly with OEMs. In aerospace it is largely Tier-2, with some direct OEM work. In nuclear it is mostly Tier-2 where EPC contractors are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear margins and the nuclear mix two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose segment margins. Consolidated EBITDA margin is guided at 30-32%+ long run and about 34-35% for FY27. Four new nuclear reactors are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Hobel Bellows revenue and margin, and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hobel contributed about INR22 crore over two months. Segment margin is not disclosed; consolidated EBITDA was 36.5%. Growth is guided at 15-20%, though management called it premature to treat as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income normalise, and what is the FY27 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 other income fell to INR7 crore because investable funds were deployed into the Hobel acquisition. Q2 onwards other income should be about half the Q1 level. FY26 other income was about INR46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: FACC agreement scope over two to three years, and ROCE and asset turn outlook as utilisation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: The FACC deal is a wave-specific agreement, and scope grows as new RFQs arrive. Asset turns are about 2x currently, expected at 2.5x over two to three years. ROCE of 15-16% holds for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of potential US tariffs and the QIP plan?

544322|2026-09.headline: Unimech H1 FY27 revenue rose 85% YoY to INR231 crore at 38% EBITDA margin; order book INR855 crore, up over 700% YoY.
544322|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was about INR123 crore, up 98% YoY and 14% QoQ, with Q2 PAT of about INR32 crore (24% margin). H1 PAT reached INR60 crore, up 71% YoY, and management said H1 already equals about 96% of FY26 revenue and about 94% of FY26 PAT. Management guided H2 revenue above H1 at similar margins, driven by semiconductor, nuclear and Hobel. The company said the consolidated order book is INR855 crore, of which about INR589 crore is tied to LTAs and award letters, and it flagged working capital rising toward 150-160 days by end-FY27 and a possible equity raise in early CY27.

segments.name: Aero tooling
segments.commentary: Contributed about 67% of H1 FY27 revenue; anchor business on short-cycle PO-to-PO orders, with long-term supply agreements being negotiated for high-demand tools such as engine stands.

segments.name: Precision components and assemblies (PCA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 33% of H1 revenue, of which Hobel accounted for 30% of total H1 consolidated revenue. Management said semiconductor was still small in H1 with a step-up expected in H2.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Acquired entity; integration complete, with demand from key customers strong and additional capacity requested. AS9100 certification for the Vizag facility targeted by Feb 2027.

segments.name: Dheya Engineering (associate)
segments.commentary: Unimech holds about 27% equity and exclusive manufacturing rights for micro gas turbines; Avaana Capital invested at about INR200 crore valuation on 26 Sep 2026. 40 kg thrust engine in serial production initiation.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to exceed H1 at similar margins, driven by semiconductor capital goods OEM deliveries, nuclear orders and steady run-rate in other businesses.
H1 EBITDA margin (~38%) considered sustainable for FY27; H2 margins expected to be maintained.
Aspiration of INR1,000 crore revenue, a broad indication rather than formal guidance; about 20% of that vision expected from Hobel; internal accruals sufficient for it.
Gross block expected to reach roughly INR500 crore by end FY27 including JV; asset turns of 2-2.5x cited.
Working capital days expected to move to 150-160 days by end FY27.
Over 590 qualified parts targeted by end FY27 (250+ qualified plus 340+ in throughput); 320+ parts targeted for qualification in FY27.
Saudi JV commercial manufacturing readiness targeted March or April 2027; Dheya's 20/40/50/100 kg engine variants targeted by March 2027.
Equity fundraise considered in early calendar 2027, also to help meet minimum public shareholding; needed for larger expansion, not for the INR1,000 crore vision.
capex_capacity: Facilities at about 65% utilisation, including 15-20% of capacity reserved for new production introduction, prove-outs and qualification.

Automated special process cells (anodizing, electroless nickel, passivation, zinc/cadmium plating, heat treatment, NDT) at existing facility: trials in Oct-Nov 2026, commissioning by 26 Dec 2026, Nadcap targeted 27 Mar 2027.
Saudi JV capex roughly INR200-250 crore; construction on schedule with Kanoo Group. Initial equity of about USD4 million (call transcript states USD4 billion and USD4 million in different places).
Management believes existing capacity suffices for about the next 2 years, but expansion decisions for the 3-5 year opportunity are under internal assessment; capacity build takes 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Semiconductor: one established customer and two in pipeline; 60 FAIs qualified; another 20 parts/assemblies targeted by end of calendar 2026; discussions with a Dutch semiconductor OEM for tooling.

Aerospace: three established customers and several in pipeline. Contracts include FACC (USD7.5 million, five-year aerostructure LTA, may double), a French Tier 1 door-components programme (about USD43 million over 10 years), and Honeywell (10-year LTA for engine and control-system components, extendable).
Nuclear: four new reactors in bidding stage through Tier 1 bidders, with opportunity possibly before calendar year-end; about 13-15 sub-assemblies qualified.
Management declined to disclose margins by vertical or customer, citing internal policy; directionally said to look at the overall picture rather than product-level margins.
Management said competition is not the main concern in semiconductors; scale is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of H1 revenue came from semiconductor, and what is expected in H2? Status of the semiconductor LTA?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor is small in H1, within a PCA contribution of about 33% of revenue. Management expects a step-up in H2 and further qualifications leading to an LTA; it did not quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What do the INR589 crore of LTA and award letters within the order book comprise, and when does execution start?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR589 crore is linked to FACC, Honeywell and a French Tier 1, with visibility spanning 5-10 years. Execution depends on continued qualification, supported by firm POs and exhibit forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What peak revenue can existing infrastructure support without new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no forward guidance on this. It cited a INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration, sufficient capacity for about 2 years, and asset turns of about 2-2.5x on gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 and FY29 margins be based on the H1 level?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said it is too early to set FY28-29 margins and it will guide one year at a time. H2 FY27 margins are expected to match H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dheya UAV engine revenue timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are testing the engine on their platforms, and revenue would follow that testing. Management implied FY28 or FY29 at the earliest, with serial production in 2027-28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the proposed fundraise is for the INR1,000 crore vision versus new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals are enough for the INR1,000 crore vision. The raise is for larger expansion and possibly inorganic growth, because RFQs need visible capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How do margins change as the mix shifts toward precision components?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is expected to move toward roughly 50:50 tooling and PCA at the INR1,000 crore scale. PCA carries slightly lower margins, so compression is expected, with R&D adding 1-2% margin pressure, but management does not expect a large decline.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility depends on converting qualification and first-article-inspection pipelines (250+ qualified, 340+ in throughput) into serial production; management said harvesting is mainly a FY28 event.
Working capital is set to rise from about 110 days to 150-160 days, which could pressure cash flow.
Capacity constraint risk: utilisation is about 65%, and new capex timing is still under review, with a possible equity raise in early CY27.
Dheya engine certification milestones (CDR before Dec 2026, final certification by Feb 2027) and Saudi JV commercial readiness (Mar/Apr 2027) are dated items to track.

544328|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.73% YoY to ₹128.58 crore while FY27 guidance calls for 20–25% revenue growth and ~12.5% operating EBITDA margin.
544328|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was ₹128.58 crore (up 2.73% YoY, up 27.77% QoQ) and EBITDA was ₹17.47 crore (up 0.57% YoY). FY26 turnover grew 14.39% to ₹419.54 crore, with tractors up 42.85% to ₹201.45 crore and cranes down about 3% to ₹218.09 crore. Management attributed the crane weakness to the Term III to Term V emission norm shift and steel cost spikes, and said pass-through is now complete. The new Bhud (Himachal Pradesh) pick-and-carry crane plant and a tower crane line are guided to start commercial production in Q2 FY27, after repeated delays. Several answers on order book, cash flow and the NBFC provisioning were vague or deferred to email.

financial_highlights.change: down from prior periods per analyst

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹201.45 crore (+42.85%) on 3,006 units; FY27 guided to grow 25–30%. Steady-state EBIT margin guided at about 10%. Consolidated tractor profit fell to ₹410 lakh vs ₹631 lakh standalone, attributed to NBFC NPA-norm provisioning.

segments.name: Cranes (pick-and-carry, existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹218.09 crore (about -3%) on 1,003 units; existing plant utilisation about 80%+ in FY26 vs 90%+ in FY25. FY27 guided to grow 15–20%. Q4 margin fell to about 10.4%, attributed to emission-norm cost pass-through and steel inflation.

segments.name: Tower cranes (new)
segments.commentary: Trials complete; commercial production targeted Q2 FY27. Small order book in single digits, all from north India, with ASP guided at ₹60–70 lakh (range ₹40 lakh to ₹75–80 lakh). Management guided 60–80 machines over the next six months, with 50–60% utilisation in year one.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth of about 20–25%; tractors 25–30%; existing crane plant 15–20%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at about 12.5% vs about 13% in FY26, with pressure from new products and markets.
New Bhud pick-and-carry plant to start commercial production in Q2 FY27; about 30–35% utilisation in first six months, 500–600 units minimum from that point.
Full utilisation of new pick-and-carry and tower crane capacity expected by FY28–29; 70–80% crane plant utilisation by FY29–30.
Other costs expected to settle at about 11–12% of revenue; working capital days to come under 200 by FY28–29 from about 307 days.
Internal plan of about 25% average annual growth until existing capacity is fully used.
capex_capacity: Total capex for new crane project about ₹70-plus crore, of which about ₹25 crore spent to date; balance to be spent in FY27.
Tower crane capacity of 240–250 machines per year initially, expandable without more capex (only welding machines to add).
Combined crane capacity after new plant cited as about 5,000 units (existing about 1,200 plus about 3,600 additional).
Existing tractor plant utilisation about 35% on reported volumes; management suggested 40–45% when including transmission supplied to cranes.
Bhud site: main shed steel nearly complete, pre-engineered building expected by July 2026; machine orders placed.
demand_pricing: Crane market size estimated at about 12,000–14,000 pick-and-carry units last year (management estimate, no public association data).
Company currently operates in less than half of India for cranes; crane dealer network 25+ and tractor dealer network 225+ after adding 23 in Q4.
Tractor FY26 growth was helped by a one-time custom hiring order from a southern state; export business in Nepal and Myanmar has weakened.
Export: a trial order of about 48 tractors from a German company worth about ₹6 crore; FY26 export about ₹21 crore.
About 20%+ of tractor sales financed through captive NBFC Barota; retail financing availability cited as a past constraint.
Tower crane competition is a two-player market (one foreign at 25–30% higher pricing, one Indian).

qa_highlights.question: Why did tractor volumes stay around 3,000 vs 4,500 in FY22, and why did margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY22 included a one-time southern custom hiring order and Nepal/Myanmar exports that have since weakened; retail financing constraints also held back volumes. Captive NBFC investment and financier support are expected to drive growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane margin down in Q4 and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to the emission-norm upgrade cost, only partly passed on earlier, plus a sharp steel price rise in Q4. Management says full pass-through is now done and the market will accept it from the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the crane capacity commissioning delayed and why are dealers flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Himachal monsoon delays, sand mining permission hurdles, and gas/commodity supply problems after the Middle East situation. It said the delay is not deliberate and it is confident of the planned numbers once the market is opened.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for other costs and the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Other costs rose from ₹56 crore to ₹64 crore on freight, discounts and promotions and are guided to 11–12% of revenue. Working capital days, now about 307, are expected to fall below 200 by FY28–29 as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tower crane order book and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a small order book in single digits, all from north India, with deliveries starting Q2. Margins are expected to be similar to pick-and-carry cranes, and initial margins will be low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no long-term order book; dealers replenish stock monthly, with some corporate and government orders (such as one from NTPC) on 60–90 day terms. Export was about ₹21 crore last year and a German trial order of about ₹6 crore has been received.

risks_watch: Crane plant commissioning has slipped repeatedly (October, then March, then Q2 FY27); fund utilisation about 73% as of March, with funds parked in FDRs.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided down to about 12.5% from about 13%, with the new products and markets adding pressure.
Crane dealer count was flat quarter-on-quarter at 25+ per the analyst, and management has not yet shown tower crane deliveries.
Market oversupply risk: new capacity of about 3,600 units is roughly 25–30% of the estimated 12,000–14,000 unit pick-and-carry market.
Consolidated cash flow fell from about ₹53 crore to about ₹30 crore; management deferred the explanation to email.
NBFC NPA-norm change requires higher provisioning, reducing consolidated tractor profit.

544328|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.
544328|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore and EBITDA rose 10.84% to ₹13.09 crore. Tractor revenue grew 36.29% to ₹52.08 crore, while crane revenue was flat at ₹52.86 crore, which management attributed to the Tier III to Tier V emission norm transition and full utilisation of the existing crane plant. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. The new Bhud plant is targeted for commercial production by end-November 2026, with tower crane production planned for the new line.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.08 crore, up 36.29% YoY. Management guides 25–30% FY27 growth; utilisation of ~12,000-unit capacity is about 35–40%, and no capacity addition planned. Dealer network about 225.

segments.name: Cranes
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.86 crore, flat YoY. Existing plant at full capacity (~1,000–1,200 units); guidance 15–20% FY27 growth from existing plant. Dealer network about 25, stagnant for three quarters. New Bhud plant capacity 3,600 units.

Standalone EBITDA margin 12.5–13% for FY27; consolidated margin said to be similar to last year (~14–15% per analyst’s reading).

Crane price hike taken; further price hike planned in coming months; management expects cost pass-through from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane dealer count stagnant at 25, and what is the plan to absorb new capacity?

qa_highlights.question: What is the crane sales volume and YoY volume growth in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management said figures would be shared by email via the Finance Head.

544335|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR820 crore and PAT rose 77.8% to INR44.92 crore; order book stood at about INR1,235 crore at 31 March 2026.
544335|2026-03.overview: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure reported FY26 revenue from operations up 61% YoY to INR820 crore, with EBITDA (excluding other income) up about 82% to INR75 crore and EBITDA margin up 105 bps to 9.13%. H2 FY26 revenue was INR478 crore (up 61% YoY) with EBITDA of INR47.48 crore at a 9.93% margin. Management said the order book declined YoY to about INR1,235 crore, which it attributed to bidding for larger-ticket projects and faster execution. The company also flagged a preferential warrant issue of up to INR13.09 crore, higher borrowing limits, a maiden dividend of INR0.25 per share, and entry into wastewater civil works.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, urban)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EPC EBITDA margin of about 14% for FY26 (13-15% range), up from 12-13% last year. FY26 revenue split by business: road/EPC about 49%, RMC about 3%, toll collection about 47%. Sector revenue cited: road/building EPC about INR395 crore, RMC about INR20 crore, wastewater about INR6 crore, toll about INR388 crore.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: Toll EBITDA margin about 4% in FY26 (about 3% last year); management also cited a toll segment margin of about 2.5%. Toll strike rate is above 70%. Recent NHAI toll awards include Kathpur INR91.71 crore, Simliya INR86.7 crore, Aashpur INR70.39 crore, Khambara INR47.83 crore, Paraghat INR33.27 crore.

segments.name: Wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Entered in FY26 with a Tamil Nadu project of about INR167 crore; wastewater order book about INR162 crore. Management cited a 15-20% EBITDA margin for the vertical, but work is currently subcontracted or on name-lending basis with no technology tie-up. Target contribution of 20-25% of revenue in the near future.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete and real estate
segments.commentary: RMC revenue about INR20 crore in FY26. Residential plotting in Indore has about 1.8 lakh sq ft unsold inventory, with WIP/inventory about INR15 crore. The company also holds a 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP, a Indore commercial real-estate build with about 3-3.5 lakh sq ft saleable area and expected revenue of about INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20-25% revenue growth annually; for FY27 it aims for EBITDA margin of 10-11% against 9.13% in FY26 (about 9-9.25% blended in its margin discussion).
Top FY27 priority is order inflow of about INR2,000 crore, across roads, wastewater and toll contracts.
Bids of about INR1,500-2,000 crore are pending opening; about INR2,500 crore of orders identified for bidding in the current month.
Bid capacity cited at about INR2,000 crore; individual EPC bid capacity INR600-700 crore; building about INR150 crore; toll collection described as unlimited based on net worth.
Plans to bid PPP, HAM and BOT projects in the current fiscal, including NHAI asset monetisation of about 17 road projects.
Management said it would not commit to the projected INR1,000-1,200 crore of project completions in FY27.
capex_capacity: Equipment base of 230+ construction equipment and vehicles; workforce above 1,100 employees.
Operates 37 ongoing projects across nine states; executed more than 40 projects in total.
Preferential issue of convertible warrants up to INR13.09 crore approved; proceeds targeted at working capital needs in about 10-12 months.
Borrowing limits enhancement proposed to support larger projects.
Acquired 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP (Indore real-estate build, completion in about 2-2.5 years).
demand_pricing: Management said tender flow has not slowed; the YoY order book decline reflects a shift to larger projects and faster execution of earlier orders, with about INR811 crore executed in FY26.
Strike rate: about 10-15% in EPC road building and above 70% in toll collection contracts.
Wastewater competition is intensifying: for a INR200 crore BUIDCO bid there were 15-20 bidders; the company was L2 in one and L3 in another bid.
Fuel and crude price volatility: force majeure and price-escalation clauses are being invoked; management says a short-term hit of about 1-1.5 months has since stabilised.
Company prefers centrally funded projects (NHAI, NHIDCL, MoRTH); working capital cycle cited at 30-45 days.
Company prefers large tickets: NH projects above INR500 crore and building projects above INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall YoY, and is tender flow slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no slowdown; the company is bidding for larger projects and executed INR811 crore in FY26 against a INR1,313 crore opening order book. It said about INR1,500-2,000 crore has been bid and is not yet opened.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should investors expect going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended EBITDA margin is 9-9.25% currently; FY26 toll EBITDA was about 4% and EPC about 14%. Target for the current year is 10-11% blended.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wastewater margin, and how will mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater EBITDA margin was cited at 15-20%. Management expects wastewater at about 20-25% of revenue in the near future, with the balance from roads, buildings, RMC and toll. It is currently subcontracting or name-lending because it lacks credentials.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split across business lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 revenue split of about 49% road, 3% RMC, 47% toll, with wastewater very small. Road and toll drove the growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to fuel price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts include force majeure and price-variation provisions; some agencies have issued SOPs, and the company expects price variations to offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest opportunities and risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Opportunities cited are large TOT-model toll contracts of INR1,500-2,000 crore and the return of BOT projects. Execution risk remains, though management said it has 40 years of experience and works in nine states.

risks_watch: Order book fell YoY to about INR1,235 crore; conversion of about INR1,500-2,000 crore pending bids is key to FY27 growth.
Wastewater margin claims (15-20%) are unproven; the company lacks credentials and works as subcontractor or name-lender; competition is intense.
Management declined to commit to FY27 completions of INR1,000-1,200 crore, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
Toll segment margin (about 2.5-4%) is much lower than EPC, so mix shift toward toll dilutes margin.
Operating cash flow was negative in FY25 and turned positive in FY26; sustainability is management's expectation, not guaranteed.
Management did not provide an order book figure as of 31 May 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Entry into wastewater civil works with a INR167 crore Tamil Nadu project and a target of 20-25% of revenue, though the vertical is currently subcontracted or name-lent with no technology tie-up.

rows.why: Bid capacity is about INR2,000 crore and INR1,500-2,000 crore of bids are pending opening, but the order book fell YoY and no bid results are yet known.

rows.why: Management plans to bid these in the current fiscal and cites TOT toll contracts of INR1,500-2,000 crore, but answers were broad and aspirational with no committed pipeline.

rows.label: Warrant proceeds for working capital and cash flow sustainability
rows.why: Preferential warrants up to INR13.09 crore target working capital, and operating cash flow was negative in FY25 and turned positive in FY26, which management has not guaranteed.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20-25% growth and the 10-11% margin target and on tender flow, but cautious and evasive on FY27 completions and segment margin and mix figures; analysts pressed on the falling order book and wastewater credentials.

544339|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.
544339|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

financial_highlights.change: Minor sequential improvement; ~76% excluding scanner sales
vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance incl. investments

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, with international lab up 40.9% YoY and domestic lab up 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore. Digital penetration in domestic lab is about 80%, with a medium-term target above 90%.

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

risks_watch: US tariff regime remains volatile. Current 10% rate could change, and the US is about 20% of revenue.
Freight costs and global shipping disruption caused Vedia export delays, which could recur at quarter-end.
Bizdent faces pricing pressure from domestic and funded competitors. Management is weighing margin against growth.
Gross margin is diluted by scanner sales, which carry lower margins. Scanner margin trajectory matters for consolidated margin.
Management has not reaffirmed the earlier margin targets. Watch whether FY27 margins hold at Q4 levels.
Kids-e-Dental international registration timing is uncertain.
Recent labour code changes affected Q3 gratuity and tax; Q4 PAT included a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit that will not recur.
