key_quotes: we close the year with a strong exit quarter, delivering highest ever quarterly numbers across key metrics.

Scanner business is for us an enabler.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation
vs INR14.8 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.

Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?

544342|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.4% to INR 434.12 crore and PAT 35.61% to INR 43.84 crore; management reiterates 30-35% CAGR target.
544342|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total revenue of INR 434.12 crore (+14.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 61.35 crore (+23.34%) and PAT of INR 43.84 crore (+35.61%), against an internal target of INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT. The Bhilwara 10,000 MT R-32 plant received environmental clearance and is guided to start production by October 2026. Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore was flat-to-down versus prior quarters, which analysts questioned; management attributed this to LPG and energy disruptions hitting end-customer industries. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR and 3-4% margin improvement over three years, with FY27 PAT guided at about INR 100 crore and a 2030 aspiration of INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR target of 30-35% over next three years with margin improvement of 3-4%.

FY27 revenue: management cited about INR 275 crore from R-32 over six months of operation plus the existing business, implying about INR 430 crore base; FY27 PAT estimated at about INR 100 crore (40 crore base plus about 60 crore from new capacity at 22% PAT).
H1 FY27 PAT margins expected to be similar to last year's levels; H2 margins expected to rise about 5-6 percentage points as manufacturing (22-24% PAT margin) contributes about 50% of growth.

HFO manufacturing plant: management said to start after Bhilwara is stabilised (post mid-FY27); no further dilution envisaged after the rights issue.
Company operates four facilities with two more under development, supported by a pan-India distribution network.

Management expects Indian refrigerant/air-conditioning demand to grow 10-15% YoY for the next 10 years; Indian market for R-32 cited at 20,000-22,000 MT.
Industry capacity: management cited about 40,000-50,000 MT of additional R-32 capacity coming up in India, designed largely for exports; China HFC capacity cited at about 800,000 MT.
Q4 top-line flat-to-lower attributed to LPG shortages and supply-chain disruption hitting end-customer industries rather than pricing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said shares sold were bought back, and the dilution (about 68%) reflected an issue price of INR 99 rather than the INR 140 initially planned; current holding stated at about 47.5% or a little more.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT for FY26, which was surpassed; 30-35% growth is for the next three years; FY27 needs about INR 560 crore for 30% growth and is expected to exceed it if R-32 starts on time.

qa_highlights.answer: Company pays 20-30% advances only, with balance on delivery and commissioning; orders placed for almost all equipment, so payments should rise significantly this quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sharjah Oxygen tie-up is strategic; Qatar helium output is curtailed, but helium prices have risen sharply, which management views as an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the R32 plant delayed and what funding was used?
qa_highlights.answer: A planned preferential issue was abandoned after a share-price spike; a rights issue was used instead, reaching the market only by February, so the planned December startup slipped to March-end under the original plan.

qa_highlights.question: What are the helium volumes and how is supply secured given Middle East shipping disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~5 containers in FY27, 12 in FY28, 24 after; utilisation about 20% of 1,200 MTPA next year. Supply secured via Sharjah Oxygen, swap arrangements and multiple sources; price expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity or debt for the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it previously preferred internal accruals, but now sees dilution and debt as likely for faster growth ('some dilution, some debt, not all debt'); no decision made yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much R32 volume is pre-sold under contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose pre-sales, calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs; said the company will not commit to take-or-pay contracts ahead of plant readiness.

risks_watch: R32 Bhilwara completion slipped from July 2026 to end-December 2026 after funding delays; FY27 R32 contribution (earlier ₹250 crore) expected to change, with Q4 FY27 revenue around ₹125 crore; watch for further slippage and commissioning updates next quarter.
Q1 FY27 margins described by management as a special quarter, with about 50% of EBITDA from inventory gains; FY27 PAT margin ex-R32 seen around 10%, so margin normalisation is a key risk.

Funding: management moved from no-dilution stance to considering some dilution and some debt for faster growth; no decision yet. Watch for fund-raise announcements and working capital needs as Khalapur, Mambattu and R32 go live together.

Helium supply constraint from Middle East shipping disruption; management relies on Sharjah Oxygen tie-ups and swap arrangements, and expects higher prices for 2-3 years. Helium plant commercial start expected next quarter.

R32 pricing downtrend (about ₹800/kg vs ~₹900 peak) against guidance based on ₹550/kg; no contracted or take-or-pay offtake disclosed for R32 volumes, with management calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs.
Mambattu scope expanded to 12 tanks and now due by year-end; HFO plant (₹350-400 crore, 10,000 tons) pending EC approval of about six months, with announcement expected towards year-end.
key_quotes: Those are not the actual numbers at our current business level that we enjoy.
It would change a little bit.
Now we are close to the idea that we might go for dilution onwards.
We would go public I think towards the end of the year after this plant is successfully commissioned is when we would go in full swing for the HFO plant, not before.
544342|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term 30-35% revenue CAGR, Khalapur helium and R32 demand, but cautious on near-term margins, which management called a special quarter. Notably evasive on pre-sold R32 volumes and on the AHF raw-material source, and more open than before on the possibility of dilution and debt.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA up 75.85% to ₹25.27 crore with ~50% from inventory gains that management calls a 'special quarter'; FY27 PAT margin ex-R32 seen around 10%, but medium-term EBITDA margin guided up 3-4% as backward integration and helium scale.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (helium commercial ops next quarter); Q4 FY27 (R32 e
rows.why: Khalapur 1,200 MTPA helium plant is complete with commercial ops next quarter, Bhilwara 10,000 MT R32 slipped from July 2026 to end-December 2026, and Mambattu HFO blending is due by year-end, though each has already slipped once.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides helium to ~5 containers in FY27, 12 in FY28 and 24 thereafter (about 20% utilisation of 1,200 MTPA next year), and R32 at ₹500-600 crore in FY28; 30-35% revenue CAGR held.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management plans roughly one new plant per year for three years and a proposed 10,000-ton HFO plant at ₹350-400 crore is pending EC approval of about six months, with announcement guided for year-end after R32 commissioning; utilisation not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 30-35% revenue CAGR but cut the FY27 R32 contribution from ₹250 crore to a Q4 run-rate of ~₹125 crore and R32 prices fell to ~₹800/kg from ~₹900 peak, against a ₹550/kg guidance basis.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: R32 commissioning has already slipped from July 2026 to end-December 2026, FY27 R32 contribution was trimmed from ₹250 crore, and the Q1 margin is called a special quarter that will not repeat.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: High-purity helium commercial start next quarter (~5 containers in FY27 rising to 12 in FY28), R32 Bhilwara by end-December 2026, and Mambattu HFO blending with hydrocarbon and helium capability by year-end.

rows.label: Funding for expansion: dilution and debt
rows.why: Management moved from preferring internal accruals to 'some dilution, some debt, not all debt' for faster growth, with no decision yet; the R32 funding delay already pushed the plant from July 2026 to end-December 2026.

rows.label: R32 offtake not contracted
rows.why: Management declined to disclose pre-sales, called existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs, and will not commit to take-or-pay ahead of plant readiness, so R32 revenue rests on uncontracted demand against 70,000-90,000 t of coming Indian capacity versus ~20,000 t demand.

rows.label: R32 price correction
rows.why: R32 price has fallen to ~₹800/kg from ~₹900 peak while guidance assumes ₹550/kg, though helium is stable at ~₹4,000/kg and management expects shortfall-driven price rises for 2-3 years.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 30-35% revenue CAGR, Khalapur helium and R32 demand, but cautious that Q1 margins were a special quarter with about 50% of EBITDA from inventory gains; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, pre-sold R32 volumes and the funding route.

544343|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore (from INR99.7 crore), with EBITDA flat at INR35.80 crore and FY27 guidance of minimum 35% growth.
544343|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 9.4% to INR115.60 crore and revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore, which management said was below internal expectations as enterprise decision cycles elongated and large ramp-ups slipped into FY27. EBITDA was INR35.80 crore versus INR35.69 crore, with the margin (31%, computed on total income including other income of about INR10.55 crore) moderating on Middle East investments, Gurgaon expansion, senior hires and AI build-out. PAT fell to INR25.50 crore from INR25.80 crore and basic EPS to INR10.44 from INR11.83, partly on a full-year post-IPO share count. The company remains debt-free with about INR171.3 crore of cash and investments, and announced a proposed acquisition of Epitome Cloud Inc. for about INR40 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35.69 crore in FY25; margin 31% on total income incl. other income
vs INR25.80 crore in FY25; PAT margin 22.1%
mainly FD interest and sale of current investments
cash and bank INR88.62 crore, current investments INR81.13 crore, LT FDs approx. INR1.6 crore

segments.name: AI / ML / GenAI
segments.commentary: AI-related revenue exceeded 10% of total company revenue for the first time in FY26. Management said all AI contracts start as fixed-cost discovery and move to T&M on production.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: US approx. 41%, Europe and UK approx. 31%, Middle East approx. 11%, India approx. 10%, rest of world approx. 7%. Management has pulled back Middle East trade-show spend and new-logo acquisition for now.

segments.name: Engagement model
segments.commentary: About 91% of FY26 revenue came from time-and-material engagements; the remaining about 9% was limited-period fixed-cost work.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: minimum 35% revenue growth in INR terms, described by management as a pessimistic case and subject to revision; no split between organic and inorganic.
EBITDA margin to recover gradually toward 33%, with management also referring to at least 200 bps improvement; the margin basis includes other income.
Three-year goal of about INR200 crore top line while maintaining and improving the EBITDA margin.

Epitome Cloud acquisition: consideration about INR40 crore, target revenue about INR28-30 crore, expected to add 25-30% to revenue; completion expected in 8-12 weeks, funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals with no external debt.
Management plans two to three further acquisitions (AI with fintech or healthtech vertical focus).
Dividend: interim 10% of face value paid and final 10% proposed; management said payout to be around 20-25% of profit. No buyback planned for now.
capex_capacity: Development centres in Kolkata and Gurgaon; Gurgaon is the hub for new senior hires, AI and ML hiring, and management capacity building.
Onsite presence in Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Morocco; Middle East staff are deployed through a third-party provider, which shows up in technical fees.
Epitome Cloud brings about 55 people (7 onsite in US, about 45 in India) and is run as-is post-acquisition; Epitome revenue is about INR28 crore on a CY26 basis.
Management expects to set up a physical office in the US after the acquisition.
Investments in AI capability, leadership hiring and enterprise sales were expensed, not capitalised, per the CFO.
demand_pricing: Client retention about 90%; management expects about 10% churn and net new revenue of INR20-25 crore organically in FY27.
Two Fortune 500 wins in FY26 (life sciences/healthcare with domain analytics and warehouse management; chemicals and materials with UiPath automation).
Nine international trade shows in FY26, six in the Middle East; about 500 qualified leads generated, and deal cycles of 6-12 months mean conversions are still pending.
Trade-show commitments reduced to two or three major events for FY27 with spend redirected to a new outbound demand-gen team and US/UK/Europe events.
Middle East: one of the top five clients is in the region, with BFSI as the only vertical there; the company is holding off on net new logos in the region.
Management cited global economic uncertainty as the biggest sector headwind, plus AI talent availability; it cited increasing demand for AI, cloud modernisation and automation.

qa_highlights.question: Why has organic growth been weak, and what is the acquisition cost and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Epitome is about INR40 crore consideration, INR28-30 crore revenue, and 25-30% of revenue contribution. Organic growth of INR20-25 crore net new is expected after about 10% churn; 35% is the most pessimistic case.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin 31% when the reported EBITDA is about INR25 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the margin uses total income including other income (about INR10.55 crore) as the denominator. Excluding other income the EBITDA margin is about 34%, so the reported 31% is on the total-income basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why were trade-show and marketing costs reduced, and why did other expenses rise about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East trade-show commitments were cut because of the West Asia situation and spend was redirected to demand gen, US/UK/Europe events. Other expenses rose because Middle East staff are supplied via a third party (technical fees) and marketing spend was reallocated, not cut.

qa_highlights.question: What are the parameters for M&A and Epitome's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four criteria: services company with some IP, majority export revenue, profitable and growing, and a technology or domain specialisation. The CFO said targets must have EBITDA margins in line with the company and bring synergy and new technology or manpower. Management said margins would improve post-deal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback given the cash position, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no buyback is planned for now, with capital directed to growth and acquisitions. The CFO said the dividend payout is intended to be about 20-25% of profit, including the final dividend, and a buyback may be reconsidered in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target breakdown and the three-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 35% is a combined organic and inorganic guidance and a three-year aim of INR200 crore top line with a stable or better margin. The CFO said the 'medium term' reference meant one year, for which 35% growth is projected.

risks_watch: Organic growth: FY26 growth was largely from pricing and the Middle East; FY27 depends on INR20-25 crore net new revenue and the slipped large ramp-ups.
Epitome integration: completion in 8-12 weeks and a Salesforce revenue-operations niche with only 7 onsite US staff; the EBITDA impact and the PAT contribution are not disclosed.
Margin: the 33% FY27 target includes other income, so operating margin is lower (about 24% ex-other income per an analyst's calculation); other income of INR10.55 crore is a large share of PBT.
Middle East: the top-five client exposure with teams no longer travelling; BFSI concentration.
Share price weakness below the IPO price and questions on shareholder returns; no buyback planned.
Use of about INR170 crore cash across acquisitions versus organic investment; capital allocation policy not fully defined.
544343|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid about the miss versus internal expectations and explained it as slipped deal closures and Middle East disruption. The tone turned assertive on the FY27 35% target, the Epitome deal and the acquisition pipeline, but was evasive on share price, buybacks and the organic growth split.
key_quotes: During the second half of financial year '26, we expected elongated enterprise decision-making cycles and delayed ramp -ups in certain large engagements, some of which now shifted into financial year '27.
So the projection that I am giving of 35% is basically the most pessimistic projection and we will revise it as the company -- as the situation evolves in the future.
Financial year 26 was the year of investment, capability building and strategic positioning of the company.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Cash and investments of ~INR171.3 cr, debt-free, and management plans 2-3 further AI/fintech/healthtech acquisitions, but no capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed; the INR40 cr Epitome deal is an acquisition, not capacity capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called 35% a pessimistic case and subject to revision, but FY26 revenue missed internal expectations as enterprise decision cycles elongated and ramp-ups slipped, so an upgrade needs evidence of conversion from 500 qualified leads with 6-12 month deal cycles still pending.

rows.why: Organic growth depends on INR20-25 cr net new revenue, Middle East (~11% of revenue, top-five client, BFSI only) new-logo acquisition is on hold, and FY26 revenue missed internal expectations.

rows.why: AI-related revenue crossed 10% of FY26 revenue for the first time and AI build-out is ongoing, but no specific product or offering launch date was named.

rows.label: Two Fortune 500 wins and pending conversions
rows.why: Two Fortune 500 wins in FY26 (healthcare analytics/warehouse management; UiPath automation) and ~500 qualified leads from 9 trade shows, but 6-12 month deal cycles mean conversions are still pending.

rows.label: Epitome Cloud acquisition and 2-3 further M&A
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for Epitome; further deals over next 2-4 quarters
rows.why: INR40 cr consideration funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals with no external debt, completion in 8-12 weeks; management plans two to three more acquisitions in AI with fintech or healthtech focus.

rows.label: Ramp-ups slipped into FY27
rows.why: Large enterprise ramp-ups slipped from FY26 into FY27 and deal cycles elongated, which supports the FY27 revenue step-up if they convert as guided.

tone.note: Management was candid about the FY26 miss and confident on the 35% FY27 target, Epitome and the M&A pipeline, but evasive on share price, buybacks and the organic vs inorganic split, which analysts pressed on alongside margin dilution and the Middle East exposure.

544344|2026-06.headline: SPR Auto Technologies Q1 FY27: consolidated total income up 51% YoY and EBITDA up 27% YoY, with PAT up 9% after higher finance costs.
544344|2026-06.overview: Management reported 51% YoY growth in consolidated total income and 27% YoY growth in consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27. Consolidated PBT rose 7% and PAT rose 9% YoY, with higher finance costs from the debt used to fund the automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin) acquisition. Management attributed a near-term margin squeeze to commodity cost pass-through lagging by about a quarter, which it said it expects to recover next quarter. Standalone legacy growth of about 12% trailed the industry, which management attributed to mix shifts and weak exports.

financial_highlights.value: INR 300 million (per investor presentation, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Powertrain-agnostic businesses share of consolidated total income

segments.name: Legacy engine components (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said manufacturing growth in the industry was about 12-14% against company growth of over 16%, though the analyst cited ~12% standalone growth. Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.

We are not going to lose on our margins.

rows.why: Management said these export markets have not yet recovered and normalisation will take more time after the West Asia situation hit exports.

544345|2026-03.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
544345|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in other current liabilities from ₹4 crores to ₹36 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹19 crores is payable to creditors for fixed assets (capex) classified as current liabilities, ~₹2 crores is year-end employee payables, and ~₹5.5 crores is advances from customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the manufacturing business and how does domestic cell sourcing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets above 15% gross/overall margin on a cost-plus model and expects at least ~15% margin to hold, though market conditions may shift over 3-6 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from the shift to lower-margin ground-mounted EPC; FY26 gross margin ~30% vs 34.5%.
Finance cost burden: ₹100 crores-plus of repayable-on-demand working capital debt; FY26 finance cost ₹10.5 crores vs ₹3.5 crores.
Working capital intensity: trade receivables up to ₹152.6 crores from ₹90.9 crores.
ALMM-II and domestic cell availability/pricing; management noted a new MNRE circular requiring monthly price declarations.
Low factory utilisation (~45%) and reliance on captive demand; conversion of the 300 MW pipeline is uncertain (a single 100 MW award is binary).
Project concentration in a 150 MW Maharashtra project; analyst noted it is a significant portion of revenue.
Inconsistent figures on call: EBITDA margin cited as ~9.5% and ~8-9%; management's FY27 guidance of 10-12% exit margin is a key test.

We do not see ALM M-II as an unmanageable constraint and in fact our manufacturing scale position us reasonably well at the broader industry transition towards the greater domestic content.

544356|2026-03.headline: AJAX FY26 revenue rose to INR2,103 crore (from INR2,074 crore) while EBITDA margin fell to 12.6%; Q4 EBITDA margin recovered to 15.1% after a 2% price hike.
544356|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue was about INR2,103 crore against INR2,074 crore in FY25, with SLCM revenue flat at INR1,758 crore on a 4% volume decline. EBITDA fell to INR266 crore (12.6% margin) from INR318 crore (15.3%), reflecting CEV5 production costs, lower operating leverage and calibrated pricing. Q4 FY26 was the turnaround quarter: revenue was flat YoY at INR758 crore, gross margin rose 170 bps to 25.8%, and EBITDA grew about 4% to INR115 crore with a 15.1% margin, helped by a 2% January price increase and direct material cost reductions. Management said it has regained market share to 73.5% in FY26 from about 69.8% in Q1, and that competitors have not taken price increases. Management gave no FY27 volume or margin guidance beyond an intent to reach early double-digit growth and 13-15% margins over the medium term.

largely flat vs FY25 despite lower volumes

EBITDA up about 4% YoY; margin up about 40 bps (management cited 14.7% base)

segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 7% in FY26 on volume growth. Management cites 4-series and 7-series pumps and 38m and 44m boom pumps, and higher-capacity batching plants as picking up.

segments.name: Spares and service
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9% in FY26 despite lower average machine running hours, supported by dealer and service network expansion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue has grown to about INR103 crore from about INR74 crore; one slipform paver sold to Saudi Arabia in March with revenue expected in Q4. Management guides 20-25% export growth for FY27.

segments.commentary: FY26 Udaan volumes about 202 units. Management says Udaan sits within SLCM and it aims for 2-3x that volume in FY27.

Medium-term aim to return to mid-teens growth and 13-15% EBITDA margin; management says FY27 achievement depends on demand, steel prices and pricing.
Working capital guidance of about 30 days as a normalised level (25-30 days as aggressive range).
Export growth of 20-25% expected for FY27.

capex_capacity: Dealer inventory about 35-40 days in most locations, with some markets 4-5 days higher on slowing demand.
Active machine population about 35,000-38,000 units; trade-in programme being built on a database of customers aged 5-8 years.

Management says it has no concrete acquisition target on the table.
demand_pricing: Central capex FY26 budget INR11.21 lakh crore, revised to INR10.96 lakh crore; utilisation about 55% until December 2025. State payment delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh constrain customer cash flow.
Price increase of 2% taken in Q4 (January), applied across the ARGO portfolio; management says peers have not taken any increase.
Management cites a 5-6% average price gap vs competitors (range 4-10%), after CEV5 transition.
Market share 73.5% in FY26; about 76% in April 2026; Oct-Dec quarter about 76-78%. Management says share held through Feb and March.
Input cost pressure from steel, fuel and cement; geopolitics, El Nino and interest rates flagged as risks.

Gujarat is strong on agrarian-to-commercial land conversion and the Commonwealth Games infrastructure; Uttar Pradesh is expected to see spending ahead of elections; Andhra Pradesh is doing well; Madhya Pradesh has no green shoots yet.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 demand outlook: can volume growth reach 15%, Udaan volumes, and state-level recovery (Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to 15%; it expects mid-to-early double-digit growth with a stronger H2. Maharashtra may turn around in H2, MP shows no green shoots, and Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan are expected to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outlook for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: A normalised 30 days is a good number for the year, with 25-30 days as an aggressive range. The key watch item is government cash flow reaching contractors and dealers.

qa_highlights.question: Will SLCM realisations rise another 1-2% on the higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: The company took a 2% price increase in Q4 and intends to recover further cost increases from the market where possible; steel and fuel costs remain pressures. No further figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 given commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The medium-term aim is 13-15% margin. Management said it is hard to predict FY27 and that holding current margins is a good outcome until volumes recover.

qa_highlights.question: Udaan volumes and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 volume was about 202 units, and management would be delighted with 2-3x that in FY27. Udaan revenue sits within SLCM.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not do turnarounds, invest where governance is weak, or enter sunset sectors. No acquisition is on the table; a decision may come in H2 and is aimed at growth through M&A or assets with quick market traction.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that competitors dump inventory at lower prices and force AJAX to reverse its price hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says competitors have had the same period to act and that the 5-6% price gap has not hurt demand. It would respond with calibrated action rather than cutting prices.

risks_watch: Government capex execution gap (about 55% utilisation to December 2025) and state payment delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh.

Steel, fuel and cement cost inflation and possible geopolitical effects on export markets (Africa, Middle East).
Working capital back-up if receivables stretch; dealer stock in some markets 4-5 days above norm.
Capital allocation: about INR1,121 crore cash with an M&A decision expected in H2 FY27; dividend policy is for the board.

544356|2026-06.headline: AJAX Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% to INR475 crores and EBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 12.5%, with SLCM market share at 75.1%.

544367|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,007 cr, +157% YoY) with 23.5% EBITDA margin, despite a INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 charge.
544367|2026-03.overview: Management reported first-ever INR 1,000 crore+ annual consolidated revenue, FY26 EBITDA of INR 236 crore (up 98%) and PAT of INR 185 crore (up 85%), above the revised guidance of about INR 900 crore revenue and 22% margin. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at about INR 310 crore total revenue, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 19.1% from 27.9% in Q3 because of a INR 25.7 crore Ind AS 29 net monetary loss at Turkish subsidiary Endoks and one-time Labour Code provisions. Order book exiting FY26 was above INR 1,400 crore. FY27 guidance is muted at about 15-20% growth as new capacity ramps, with management expecting above 50% growth in FY28.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 318 crore; margin about 20% in Q4 and 15% for the year; annualised EBIT margin about 15%. Order book about INR 430 crore; management sees only 30-35% further capacity headroom at current plant.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 468 crore; reported EBIT margin 23% including Ind AS 29 effect, about 29-30% without it; management cites about 32% EBITDA on stable-currency basis. Order book about INR 450 crore; Q4 cash flow about INR 136 crore.

segments.commentary: Turnaround underway; losses halved versus last year and management targets 70-75% growth this year without losses.

Order book target of INR 1,500-1,800 crore before start of FY27 per management.
Expect some near-term gross margin pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 from raw material and commodity price increases; pass-through to customers is with a lag.

Targeted BESS converter orders of USD 60-80 million this year against USD 31 million current BESS order book; PCS factory in Turkey (about USD 2 million investment) expected to start billing by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27.
Dividend: final dividend of INR 1 per share recommended; promoters waived their entitlement.
capex_capacity: New Sangli factory (global coil, HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire) expected to commence operations around July-August 2026; management also said trial production by end-2026 and project managers stick to Dec-Jan start; commissioning on track for Q3 FY27 per CFO.
New high-voltage test laboratory to be commissioned alongside the new factory.

Endoks: new PCS facility at Nigde targeted for December 2026; new BESS manufacturing facility on in-house technology; 1,725 kW PCS inverter expected to launch within next two quarters.
Capital WIP of INR 73 crore; management says Sangli peak revenue potential of about INR 1,500 crore subject to CTC cable expansion and insulator supply.

BESS: management sees BESS PCS as 40-50% of project cost; converter margins about 10-12% at bid level, targeted to reach 17-18% at volume; battery pass-through about 2-3%.

Data centres: first US data-centre order of about INR 49 crore won; management expects a couple more projects in coming quarters; US reactor market for data centres sized at about INR 1,500 crore per year by management.

Supply chain constraints: insulator deliveries running 18-24 months; cable constraints mitigated by vertical integration. Order intake in Sangli and Delhi largely closed for next quarter; only strategic orders being taken.
Transformer bids in US (USD 80-100 million) were largely lost; management is not prioritising transformers at lower margins.

544397|2026-03.headline: Ather's FY26 volumes rose ~66% with Q4 at 83,000 units; Q4 EBITDA loss narrowed to about -2% of revenue, while commodity inflation is expected to pressure margins near term.
544397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a breakthrough year, with volumes up about 66% led by Rizta (almost three-quarters of sales) and market share up from about 8% to 18.6% in Q4. Store count doubled from 351 to 700 by March 2026, and AGM with subsidy improved from 19% to 24% (about 12% to 21% without subsidy) on COGS reduction of about 9 percentage points. Q4 EBITDA loss improved about 2,000 bps to roughly -2%. Management flagged sharp commodity inflation (lithium, rare earth magnets, memory, aluminium) that will pressure margins in the short term, with only a small part passed on so far, and said the Factory 3.0 (AURIC) and EL platform are the key FY27 levers.

financial_highlights.change: up ~23% QoQ per analyst question/management reference to volume growth
highest ever; rose through the year

segments.name: Middle India (Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, MP, Odisha, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Market share rose from about 4% at start of FY25 to 17.3%; store additions up 125% YoY. Gujarat and Odisha at about 19-20%, Maharashtra at 16%+ from about 8%.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Market share moved from 13% to 23% with 80% more stores; quarterly sales rose from about 27,000 to about 41,000 units. Kerala Pro-Pack attach about 98-99%.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Market share tripled from just under 4% to about 12%; Rest of India Pro-Pack attach at 81%, the weakest zone.

guidance_outlook: EL platform (mass and mass-premium focus, INR1-1.25 lakh segment where Ather has no product) to be commercialised by festive season and in the field before end of CY26; management said no exact launch month given.

Factory 3.0 (AURIC, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar): Phase 1 of 5 lakh units capacity (10 lakh total) to start trial production before end CY26 and 42,000 units/month incremental capacity fully operational before end FY27; first revenue from new factory expected in Q4 FY27.
Cost reduction to come mainly from EL over FY27 (more back-loaded); 450/Rizta platform cost reduction to be smaller than prior two years.

Short-term margin pressure expected from commodity inflation (commodity cost inflation estimated at 40-50%, BOM increase a fraction of that); further price hike possible in coming months after roughly INR4,000 blended hikes in CY26 so far.
FAME subsidy expiry in coming months to reduce realisation by about INR5,000 per vehicle.
No specific new-store guidance for FY27; management expects the current quarterly EC opening pace to broadly continue.

AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase 1: 5 lakh capacity out of 10 lakh planned; adds 42,000 units/month; trial production before end CY26.
Factory 3.0 to add in-house battery pack assembly, transmission assembly, painting, electronics assembly and CED coating, raising vertical integration.
Hosur plant moved to triple-shift operation, adding depreciation.
Service centres more than doubled in FY26; store count doubled to 700.
demand_pricing: Q4 retail demand ran above estimates (retail includes units sold by dealers pending registration); supply rather than demand was the binding constraint.
Price hikes: about INR1,000-1,500 in Q4 FY26 and about INR2,500 blended in April 2026, roughly INR4,000 in CY26 so far.
Q4 ASP flat QoQ; management attributed this to Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle/North India, expecting it to rise as stores mature.
Pro-Pack attach: Kerala about 98-99%, Middle India second, Rest of India 81%; Madhya Pradesh rose from 40-50% to over 80-85% within about a year.
Lithium up about 2-2.5x from around $8/kg to about $24/kg at peak, cooled somewhat; cell share of BOM rose from 15-16% (sub-20%) to a larger share.
Competition: peers have many variants across price bands while Ather has 6 premium, 3 mass-premium and no mass or entry variants.
Industry: management views the sub-INR1 lakh segment as 15-20% of market, INR1.25 lakh and above as 25-30% (top-five-OEM volumes only, indicative).

qa_highlights.question: How do Pro-Pack attach rates differ between mature South markets and newer Middle/Rest of India markets?
qa_highlights.answer: South highest (Kerala ~98-99%), then Middle India, then Rest of India at 81%; new cities start lower and reach 80%+ within two to four quarters, with existing dealer partners ramping faster (about three-quarters of new stores).

qa_highlights.question: Is 400 branch expansion in FY27 accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific FY27 store guidance; EL is the main FY27-28 growth driver and store expansion is becoming business-as-usual at the current quarterly pace.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost inflation has been passed on, and how will it be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a small part passed on so far due to procurement and stockpiling; some burden may be shared with suppliers, but the bulk is expected to fall on the company or customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 ASP flat QoQ despite the price hike and higher attach rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle and North India with lower ASPs, expecting these to normalise as stores age.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 34% and depreciation rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose on variable warranty and logistics costs with volume up, plus marketing and a year-end warranty calibration; depreciation reflects the 450 platform (seven-year life), triple-shift operation at Hosur, and useful-life recalibration of tools; EL amortisation starts next FY.

qa_highlights.question: Are there supply issues compared with competitors and when will new capacity contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Only localised constraints (Nov-Dec variants, April election-related labour disruption); no secular material shortage. New factory revenue expected in Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (lithium, aluminium, rare earths, memory) with management expecting margin pressure in the short term and limited pass-through so far.
EL launch timing (festive season or by end CY26) and Factory 3.0 Phase 1 commissioning slipping beyond CY26 / Q3 FY27.
FAME subsidy expiry removing about INR5,000 per vehicle from realisations in coming months.
Supply constraints at 90-95% utilisation of current plant limiting volume capture in South and Middle India.
Rising warranty provisions and variable other expenses; depreciation step-up as EL amortisation begins next FY.
Electric motorcycles would need a separate Zenith platform; no timeline given.

544397|2026-06.headline: Ather Energy Q1 FY27: wholesale volumes up 81% to 83,000 units, first-ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (~0.8% margin), AGM down to 22.4%.
544397|2026-06.overview: Management described a sharp demand upswing driven by policy support, fuel-availability concerns and TCO gains, with registrations up 102% YoY and paid preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh. Production was constrained at the Hosur plant (35,000 units/month max, reached near full utilisation by June), leaving dealer inventory at about 3 days versus 14 days earlier. Commodity costs rose sharply, cutting adjusted gross margin by 5.6 percentage points to 22.4%, partly offset by an average selling price rise to Rs 1.61 lakh and disciplined fixed-cost control that delivered the first positive EBITDA. Management expects further commodity hits of 100-200 bps, to be largely offset by price increases that were only partly reflected in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Commodity headwind: management expects a further 100-200 bps hit beyond the 5.6% in Q1, to be largely absorbed through price hikes; Q2 full-quarter ASP benefit expected.

AURIC Phase 1 (Aurangabad, Factory 3.0) go-live later in calendar 2026; expected to take total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units per year; full ramp to 42,000 units/month in 4-5 months, possibly spilling into early FY28.
EL scooter (brand name to be unveiled) launch later in August 2026; target 60,000 units/month capacity across Aurangabad and Hosur (42,000 from AURIC Phase 1 plus 18,000 from Hosur).
AURIC Phase 2 could add 5 lakh units/year (total 14.2 lakh); planning stage only, firmer timeline possibly within a quarter or two.

Ather Community Day on 29 August 2026 in Bengaluru to unveil the EL scooter.
New store openings slowed in Q1; expected to surge once EL and AURIC are live around the festive season. Stores reportedly reach operational profitability in about 5-6 months on average.
demand_pricing: Industry e-2W penetration reported at 11%, up 44%; industry registrations up 68% YoY to 525k in Q1 FY27; Ather inquiries up 95%; over 7 lakh inquiries in Q1; Ather brand searches up about 118%.

Management estimates unrealised retail potential of 13,000-15,000 units per month above the roughly 30,000 units/month retailed; some dealers have stopped accepting preorders with waits of about 2 months.
Pricing power: ASP moved from Rs 1.5 lakh (Q4) to Rs 1.53 lakh (April and May) and Rs 1.61 lakh (June), with price hikes described as 100% margin accretive.
Customer profile reportedly unchanged; retail finance and TCO advantage cited as supporting willingness to pay higher prices.
EL launch expected to depress ASP somewhat, with launch focus on northern and rest-of-India markets and attach rate guided at least 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the commodity headwind be a similar 5-6% again next quarter, or stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a further 100-200 bps of hit, not 5-6%, and says commodity costs may be near the top; quarterly averages understate end-of-quarter costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee and other expense control a new baseline before AURIC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not exceptional, reflecting cautious spending in FY27 after a strong FY26; some AURIC costs will be capitalised initially, with P&L impact from Q4 onwards alongside volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does 60,000 EL capacity relate to Hosur's 35,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: AURIC Phase 1 is dedicated to EL at 42,000/month; Hosur gives flexibility of 18,000 units/month, shared with Rizta and 450X, so total is 60,000 for EL and not additive.

qa_highlights.question: Can AURIC Phase 2 be brought forward, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is in planning; the Rs 2,500 crore raise gives funding to fast-track it, with firmer timelines possibly within one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-vehicle revenue and service?
qa_highlights.answer: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item and benefited from price increases; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for mature peers, and is expected to compound with fleet size.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ather enter electric motorcycles soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on EL platform products over the next year; a motorcycle launch is more than a year away, probably two years or more.

risks_watch: Commodity costs could rise a further 100-200 bps; margin recovery depends on price increases and commodity cooling, which management says is hard to predict.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension not yet confirmed; about 15-20% of Q1 volumes sold without subsidy.
AURIC Phase 1 ramp risk: go-live slated for later in 2026, possible slip into early FY28; supply already short of demand by about 15,000 units per month per analyst.
EL launch may lower ASP and could cannibalise Rizta; attach-rate and margin mix to be watched.

544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.name: Zones (registrations growth)
segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.name: Konarc (new mainstream scooter)
segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.
Tier 2 penetration is rising fastest; Maharashtra Tier 2 penetration is about 18-19%. Company is not yet present in rural markets.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

risks_watch: Commodity costs (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory) have stayed elevated for longer than expected; management says Q3 is unlikely to be worse than Q2, but the outlook is volatile.
The 2.7pp SKU and incentive lever is temporary and may reverse if supply eases, which could weigh on gross margin.

Capacity ramp risk: AURIC Phase 1 takes about two quarters to ramp, and the 12,000 units/month add-on is due by Q2 FY28; demand is 50,000-60,000 units/month against 77,000 installed capacity after Hosur and AURIC.
Konarc ramp and attach-rate uncertainty: early Konarc attach rates are strong, but its mix is less South-heavy, and management wants at least two quarters of data.
PAT is positive for the first time but management says it can fluctuate; PAT is not the near-term focus.

544403|2026-03.headline: ABLBL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 2,174 crores, with consolidated EBITDA up 14% to INR 375 crores and margin at 17.2%.
544403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered double-digit revenue growth of 12% YoY, led by Lifestyle Brands (+11%) and Emerging Businesses (+18%), with retail like-to-like at 6%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% to INR 375 crores and margin expanded about 20 bps to 17.2%, helped by a one-time PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores in the quarter. Reported PAT was INR 55 crores after a one-time labour code exceptional item; normalized PAT was INR 60 crores (+58%). Management flagged softer wedding demand and moderating sentiment late in the quarter from geopolitical uncertainty and volatility.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 38 crores YoY; includes one-time labour code exceptional item
vs INR 781 crores in March last year

segments.name: Emerging Business (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +18% YoY across 390+ stores; EBITDA margin up 420 bps YoY. Management puts FY26 Emerging Business EBITDA at about 4%, up from roughly breakeven last year.

segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 30%, with double-digit like-for-like for the year. Network is over 210 stores; full-year sales have more than doubled since acquisition three years ago.

segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in Q4 and sharply lower full-year losses. Management targets at least one profitable quarter in FY27, with break-even previously guided for Q4 FY26.

segments.commentary: Profitable, with double-digit like-for-like growth in the quarter.

Management flagged crude-linked input cost pressure on polyester and bottom-wear. Autumn-winter buying is largely locked; impact is not yet quantified and may lag.
Management said margin pricing power was not discussed in quantified terms; ability to pass costs through depends on how inflation plays out.

qa_highlights.question: Others channel jump and PLI benefit: what drives it and how sustainable is it?

qa_highlights.question: Store expansion: what is the FY27 pipeline and how many closures?

544403|2026-06.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
544403|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: Down ~150 bps YoY per analyst question; management called it marginally lower

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,725 crore (+10% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 319 crore at 18.5% margin. Retail grew 10% with 7% LFL across almost 3,000 stores; e-commerce grew 23% group-wide and over 50% on the company's own platform.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.name: Channels (group)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.

Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.

Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

544405|2026-03.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
544405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
